title.zh: 卷二百 志第一百五十三 刑法二
title.raw: 卷二百 志第一百五十三 刑法二 Volume 200 Treatises 153: Punishment and Law 2

sentences.zh: 律令者，有司之所守也。

translations.literal: Statutes and ordinances are what the officials must uphold.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and ordinances are the province of the bureaucracy to enforce.

sentences.zh: 太祖以來，其所自斷，則輕重取舍，有法外之意焉。

translations.literal: Since Taizu, in what they decided for themselves, severity, leniency, acceptance, and rejection have carried meaning beyond the law.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of Taizu onward, when emperors ruled on cases themselves, their weighing of severity and mercy often carried implications outside the letter of the law.

sentences.zh: 然其末流之弊，專用己私以亂祖宗之成憲者多矣。

translations.literal: Yet the abuse at the tail end of this tendency has often been to apply private preference alone and upset the established constitutions of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In later times, however, the abuse of that discretion often meant acting on private whim and overturning the established statutes of the founding emperors.

sentences.zh: 乾德伐蜀之役，有軍大校割民妻乳而殺之，太祖召至闕，數其罪。

translations.literal: In the Qiande campaign to conquer Shu, a senior army officer cut off a commoner's wife's breast and killed her; Taizu summoned him to the palace and recounted his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande campaign against Shu, a senior army officer cut a civilian woman's breast and killed her. Taizu summoned him to court and enumerated his crimes.

sentences.zh: 近臣營求頗切，帝曰：「朕興師伐罪，婦人何辜，而殘忍至此！」

translations.literal: A nearby minister importuned him eagerly; the Emperor said: "I raised armies to punish crime—what guilt had this woman, that cruelty should go this far!"
translations.idiomatic: A courtier pressed eagerly for leniency. The Emperor said, "I raised armies to punish wrongdoing—what had this woman done to deserve cruelty like this?"

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: He then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him executed at once.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣吏承五季之習，黷貨厲民，故尤嚴貪墨之罪。

translations.literal: At the time county and prefectural officials inherited the habits of the Five Dynasties, taking bribes and harming the people, so the crime of corruption was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials still followed the corrupt practices of the Five Dynasties, extorting goods and oppressing the people, so the penalties for graft were especially harsh.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，王元吉守英州 ，月餘，受贓七十餘萬，帝以嶺表初平，欲懲掊克之吏，特詔棄市。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, Wang Yuanji governed Yingzhou; in little over a month he accepted bribes of more than seven hundred thousand; the Emperor, because the Lingnan region had just been pacified and wishing to punish extortionate officials, specially ordered execution at the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 4, Wang Yuanji served as prefect of Yingzhou and within little more than a month took bribes exceeding seven hundred thousand cash. Because the far south had only recently been pacified, the Emperor wished to make an example of grasping officials and issued a special order for public execution.

sentences.zh: 陝州民范義超，周顯德中，以私怨殺同里常古真家十二口，古真小子留留幸脫走，至是，擒義超訴有司，陝州奏，引赦當原。

translations.literal: A commoner of Shanzhou, Fan Yichao, in the Xiande era of Zhou, killed twelve members of his fellow townsman Chang Guzhen's household from private enmity; Guzhen's young son Liuliu fortunately escaped; at this time Yichao was captured and appealed to the authorities; Shanzhou memorialized that under amnesty he should be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yichao, a commoner of Shanzhou, had killed twelve members of his neighbor Chang Guzhen's household out of private spite during the Zhou Xiande era. Guzhen's young son Liuliu had fortunately escaped. Now Yichao was seized and brought before the authorities. Shanzhou reported that an amnesty should absolve him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈有殺一家十二人，可以赦論邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How can one who killed twelve people of a single household be discussed under pardon?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Can a man who slaughtered twelve people in one family really be pardoned?"

sentences.zh: 命正其罪。

translations.literal: He ordered that his crime be properly assessed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the proper penalty applied.

sentences.zh: 八年，有司言：「自三年至今，詔所貸死罪凡四千一百八人。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the authorities said: "From the third year until now, those whose capital crimes were commuted by edict number altogether four thousand one hundred eighteen persons."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the authorities reported, "From the third year to the present, edicts have commuted capital sentences for a total of 4,118 persons."

sentences.zh: 帝注意刑辟，哀矜無辜，嘗嘆曰：「堯、舜之時，四凶之罪止於投竄。

translations.literal: The Emperor paid attention to punishments, pitied the innocent, and once sighed: "In the time of Yao and Shun, the crimes of the Four Evildoers stopped at banishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept a close eye on criminal justice and pitied the innocent. He once sighed, "In the age of Yao and Shun, even the Four Evildoers were punished only with exile.

sentences.zh: 先王用刑，蓋不獲已，何近代憲網之密耶！」

translations.literal: When former kings applied punishments, it was surely because they had no choice—how is it that recent times' legal nets are so dense!"
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings used punishment only when they had no alternative—why are the laws of recent times so tight?"

sentences.zh: 故自開寶以來，犯大辟，非情理深害者，多得貸死。

translations.literal: Therefore from Kaibao onward, those who committed capital offenses, unless deeply harmful in sentiment and reason, mostly obtained commutation of death.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaibao onward, most offenders facing death unless their crimes were extraordinarily heinous in motive and effect had their sentences commuted.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，自春涉夏不雨，太宗意獄訟濫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, from spring through summer there was no rain; Taizong suspected that litigation was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 6, drought lasted from spring into summer, and Taizong suspected that the courts were overburdened with cases.

sentences.zh: 會歸德節度推官李承信因市笞園戶，病創死。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Chengxin, judicial aide of the Guide military commission, beat a garden tenant in the marketplace over a dispute; the man died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time, Li Chengxin, a judicial aide on the Guide military commission, beat a gardener in a market dispute, and the man died of his injuries.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，坐承信棄市。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he had Chengxin executed at the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of it, the Emperor had Chengxin executed in public.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖嘗決繫囚，多得寬貸。

translations.literal: Earlier, Taizu had once decided cases of imprisoned persons and mostly granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taizu reviewed prisoners, he had often shown mercy.

sentences.zh: 而開封婦人殺其夫前室子，當徒二年，帝以其凶虐殘忍，特處死；

translations.literal: But when a Kaifeng woman killed her husband's son by a former wife, the statute called for two years' penal servitude; the Emperor, because she was vicious and cruel, specially ordered death;
translations.idiomatic: When a Kaifeng woman killed her stepson, the statute called for two years' penal servitude, but the Emperor, finding her conduct vicious and cruel, ordered her executed;

sentences.zh: 至是，有涇州安定婦人，怒夫前妻之子婦，絕其吭而殺之，乃下詔曰：「自今繼母殺傷夫前妻子，及姑殺婦者，同凡人論。」

translations.literal: at this time a woman of Anding in Jingzhou, enraged at her husband's son by a former wife's daughter-in-law, cut her throat and killed her; he then issued an edict: "From now on, when a stepmother kills or injures her husband's children by a former wife, or when a mother-in-law kills her daughter-in-law, they are to be judged like ordinary persons."
translations.idiomatic: Now a woman in Anding, Jingzhou, enraged at her stepson's wife, cut her throat and killed her. The Emperor then decreed, "From now on, stepmothers who kill or injure their husbands' children by a former marriage, and mothers-in-law who kill their daughters-in-law, shall be tried like anyone else."

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，開封寡婦劉使婢詣府，訴其夫前室子王元吉毒己將死，右軍巡推不得實，移左軍巡掠治，元吉自誣伏，俄劉死，及府中慮囚，移司錄司案問，頗得其侵誣之狀，累月未決，府白于上，以其毒無顯狀，令免死，決徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, the Kaifeng widow Liu sent a maid to the prefectural office to accuse her husband's son by a former wife, Wang Yuanji, of poisoning her so she would die; the Right Army Patrol could not establish the facts and transferred the case to the Left Army Patrol for coercive interrogation; Yuanji confessed under duress; soon Liu died; when the prefecture reviewed prisoners, the case was transferred to the Judicial Recorder's office for investigation, and they largely obtained the facts of false accusation; after many months it was still unresolved; the prefecture reported upward that because there was no clear evidence of poisoning, he was to be spared death and sentenced to penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 1, a Kaifeng widow named Liu sent a servant to the prefectural court to accuse her stepson Wang Yuanji of poisoning her. The Right Army Patrol could not prove the charge and handed the case to the Left Army Patrol, who tortured Yuanji until he confessed. Liu soon died. When the prefecture reviewed its prisoners, the Judicial Recorder's office took up the case and largely uncovered a false accusation, but months passed without a resolution. The prefecture reported upward that, with no clear proof of poisoning, Yuanji should be spared death and sentenced to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 元吉妻張擊登聞鼓稱，帝召問張，盡得其狀，立遣中使捕元推官吏，御史鞫問，乃劉有姦狀，慚悸成疾，懼其子發覺而誣之，推官及左、右軍巡使等削任降秩，醫工詐稱被毒，劉母弟欺隱王氏財物及推吏受贓者，並流海島，餘決罰有差。

translations.literal: Yuanji's wife Zhang struck the Petition Drum at the palace gate; the Emperor summoned and questioned Zhang and fully obtained the facts; he immediately sent a palace envoy to arrest the original investigating officials; the Censorate interrogated them and found that Liu had been conducting an affair, became ill from shame and fear, and, afraid her stepson would discover it, falsely accused him; the judicial aide and the Left and Right Army Patrol commissioners had their appointments stripped and ranks reduced; the physician who falsely claimed she had been poisoned, Liu's younger brother by her mother who concealed the Wang family's property, and investigating clerks who took bribes were all exiled to island penal colonies; the rest received punishments of varying severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji's wife Zhang beat the Petition Drum. The Emperor summoned her, learned the full story, and at once sent a palace envoy to seize the original investigators. The Censorate found that Liu had been carrying on an affair, fell ill from shame and fear, and, afraid her stepson would expose her, had framed him. The judicial aide and the Left and Right Army Patrol commissioners were demoted; the physician who falsely claimed poisoning, Liu's uterine brother who had concealed the Wang family's property, and clerks who took bribes were all exiled to island penal colonies; others were punished according to their roles.

sentences.zh: 司錄主吏賞緡錢，賜束帛。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the Judicial Recorder's office was rewarded with cash strings and given bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk of the Judicial Recorder's office was rewarded with cash and given bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 初元吉之繫，左軍巡卒繫縛搒治，謂之「鼠彈箏」，極其慘毒。

translations.literal: When Yuanji was first imprisoned, Left Army Patrol soldiers bound and beat him in a method called the "rat-on-a-zither," to the utmost cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji was first imprisoned, the Left Army Patrol bound and beat him with a torture called the "rat-on-a-zither," inflicting extreme cruelty.

sentences.zh: 帝令以其法縛獄卒，宛轉號叫求速死，及解縛，兩手良久不能動。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that the same method be used on the prison guards; writhing, they cried out begging for a quick death; when unbound, their hands could not move for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had the same method applied to the guards. Writhing, they screamed for a quick death. When they were untied, their hands could not move for a long while.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相曰：「京邑之內，乃復酷如此，况四方乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the chief ministers: "Within the capital it is still this cruel—how much more so in the four directions!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told his chief ministers, "If it is this cruel in the capital, what must it be like everywhere else?"

sentences.zh: 端拱間，虜犯邊郡，北面部署言：「文安、大城二縣監軍段重誨等棄城遁，請論以軍法。」

translations.literal: During the Duanhong era, barbarians invaded border prefectures; the Northern Frontier Command reported: "Duan Chonghui and others, military supervisors of Wen'an and Dacheng counties, abandoned their cities and fled—request that they be judged under military law."
translations.idiomatic: During the Duanhong era, when barbarians raided the frontier, the Northern Frontier Command reported that Duan Chonghui and other military supervisors of Wen'an and Dacheng had abandoned their posts and fled, and asked that they be tried under military law."

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使就斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a palace envoy to behead them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a palace envoy to execute them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 既行，謂曰：「此得非所管州軍召之邪？

translations.literal: After he had set out, the Emperor said to him: "Might this not be that the prefectural army under their command summoned them?
translations.idiomatic: After the envoy had left, the Emperor said, "Might they not have been summoned by the prefectural army that commanded them?

sentences.zh: 往訊之乃決。」

translations.literal: Go and inquire before deciding."
translations.idiomatic: Go and inquire before you decide."

sentences.zh: 使至，果訊得乾寧牒令部送民入居城，非擅離所部，遽釋之。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, he indeed learned through inquiry that a Qianning dispatch had ordered them to escort the people into the city—they had not left their posts on their own authority—and he immediately released them.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, inquiry showed that a Qianning dispatch had ordered them to move the people into the walled town—they had not deserted their posts—and he released them at once.

sentences.zh: 咸平間，有三司軍將趙永昌者，素凶暴，督運江南，多為姦贓。

translations.literal: During the Xianping era, there was a Three Departments army officer named Zhao Yongchang who was by nature fierce and violent; supervising transport in Jiangnan, he committed many acts of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, a Three Departments army officer named Zhao Yongchang was notoriously brutal. While supervising transport in the south, he committed many corrupt acts.

sentences.zh: 知饒州韓昌齡廉得其狀，乃移轉運使馮亮，坐決杖停職 。

translations.literal: The prefect of Raozhou, Han Changling, learned of his conduct through investigation and reported to the transport commissioner Feng Liang; Yongchang was sentenced to beating with the rod and suspension from office.
translations.idiomatic: Han Changling, prefect of Raozhou, investigated and reported him to transport commissioner Feng Liang. Yongchang was sentenced to beating with the rod and suspension from office.

sentences.zh: 遂撾登聞鼓，訟昌齡與亮訕謗朝政，仍偽刻印，作亮等求解之狀。

translations.literal: He then beat the Petition Drum, accusing Changling and Liang of slandering court policy, and also forged a seal and fabricated petitions in Liang's name seeking dismissal of the case.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat the Petition Drum, accusing Changling and Liang of slandering court policy, and forged a seal and fabricated petitions in Liang's name seeking to have the case dropped.

sentences.zh: 真宗察其詐，於便殿自臨訊，永昌屈伏，遂斬之，釋亮不問，而昌齡以他事貶郢州團練副使。

translations.literal: Zhenzong detected the fraud, personally interrogated him in the side hall, Yongchang confessed, and he was beheaded; Liang was released without inquiry, while Changling was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Ezhou on another matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong saw through the fraud, interrogated him personally in a side hall, and Yongchang confessed and was executed. Liang was released without further inquiry, while Changling was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Ezhou on another charge.

sentences.zh: 曹州民蘇莊蓄兵器，匿亡命，豪奪民產，積贓計四十萬。

translations.literal: A commoner of Caozhou, Su Zhuang, hoarded weapons, harbored fugitives, forcibly seized people's property, and amassed illicit gains totaling four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhuang, a commoner of Caozhou, stockpiled weapons, harbored fugitives, seized people's property by force, and amassed illicit gains totaling four hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 御史臺請籍其家，帝曰：「暴橫之民，國有常法，籍之，斯過也。」

translations.literal: The Censorate requested confiscation of his household; the Emperor said: "For violent and overbearing commoners the state has regular law—to confiscate their households would be excessive."
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate asked to confiscate his household property. The Emperor said, "For violent bullies the state already has regular penalties—to confiscate their households would go too far."

sentences.zh: 論如律。

translations.literal: He was sentenced according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced according to statute.

sentences.zh: 其縱捨輕重，必當於義，多類此。

translations.literal: Their loosening or tightening of severity always had to accord with principle—many cases were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Their loosening or tightening of punishment always had to accord with principle—many cases were like this.

sentences.zh: 凡歲饑，強民相率持杖劫人倉廩，法應棄市，每具獄上聞，輒貸其死。

translations.literal: Whenever there was famine in a year, strong commoners would band together, take up staffs, and rob others' granaries; by law they should be executed at the marketplace; each time a completed case was reported upward, death was usually commuted.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine, desperate men often banded together with clubs to raid granaries. By law they faced public execution, but whenever such cases were reported upward, death was usually commuted.

sentences.zh: 真宗時，蔡州民三百一十八人有罪，皆當死。

translations.literal: In Zhenzong's time, three hundred eighteen commoners of Caizhou were guilty and all faced death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenzong, 318 commoners of Caizhou were found guilty, all facing death.

sentences.zh: 知州張榮、推官江嗣宗議取為首者杖脊，餘悉論杖罪。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhang Rong and judicial aide Jiang Sizong deliberated to take the ringleaders and beat their backs, while the rest were all sentenced to beating.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Rong and judicial aide Jiang Sizong proposed beating only the ringleaders on the back and sentencing the rest to ordinary beating.

sentences.zh: 帝下詔褒之。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict praising them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor issued an edict praising them.

sentences.zh: 遣使巡撫諸道，因諭之曰：「平民艱食，強取餱糧以圖活命爾，不可從盜法科之。」

translations.literal: He sent envoys to tour and reassure the various circuits, instructing them: "When common people lack food, forcibly taking dry rations to try to stay alive is one thing—they must not be sentenced under the full bandit statutes."
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to tour the circuits and instructed them, "When common people lack food, seizing grain to stay alive is one thing—they must not be sentenced under the full bandit statutes."

sentences.zh: 天聖初，有司嘗奏盜劫米傷主，仁宗曰：「饑劫米可哀，盜傷主可疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng, the authorities once memorialized that bandits had robbed grain and injured the owner; Renzong said: "Robbing grain in famine is pitiable; robbing and injuring the owner is detestable.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiansheng, the authorities reported a case of grain robbery in which the owner was injured. Renzong said, "Robbing grain in famine is pitiable; robbery that injures the owner is detestable.

sentences.zh: 雖然，無知迫於食不足耳。」

translations.literal: Even so, they were ignorant people forced by insufficient food."
translations.idiomatic: Even so, they were ignorant people driven by hunger."

sentences.zh: 命貸之。

translations.literal: He ordered commutation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered their sentences commuted.

sentences.zh: 五年，陝西旱，因詔：「民劫倉廩，非傷主者減死，刺隸他州，非首謀又減一等。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Shaanxi suffered drought; an edict followed: "When commoners rob granaries, if they did not injure the owner, reduce death; tattoo and register them in another prefecture; if they were not the chief plotter, reduce one more grade."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, drought struck Shaanxi, and an edict followed: "When commoners raid granaries, if the owner was not injured, commute death; brand them and register them in another prefecture; if they were not the chief plotter, reduce the sentence one more grade."

sentences.zh: 自是，諸路災傷即降敕，饑民為盜，多蒙矜減，賴以全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever any circuit suffered disaster, an edict was issued; hungry commoners who became bandits mostly received compassionate reduction, and very many were thereby spared to live.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever any circuit suffered disaster, edicts followed, and hungry people who turned to banditry mostly received compassionate reductions—very many were spared to live.

sentences.zh: 司馬光時知諫院 ，言曰：「臣聞敕下京東、西災傷州軍，如貧戶以饑偷盜斛斗因而盜財者，與減等斷放，臣竊以為非便。

translations.literal: Sima Guang, then serving in the Remonstrance Bureau, said: "Your servant has heard that an edict was sent down to disaster-stricken prefectures and armies of Jingdong and Jingxi: when poor households steal grain measures because of famine and thereby steal property, they are to receive reduced sentencing and release—your servant privately considers this inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang, then in the Remonstrance Bureau, said, "I have heard that an edict went out to disaster-stricken prefectures in Jingdong and Jingxi: when poor households steal grain because of famine and thereby steal property, they are to receive reduced sentences and release. I believe this is unwise.

sentences.zh: 周禮荒政十有二，散利、薄征、緩刑、力、舍禁、去幾，率皆推寬大之恩以利於民，獨於盜賊，愈更嚴急。

translations.literal: The Zhou Rites' twelve famine policies—dispersing profit, lightening levies, easing punishments, employing labor, lifting prohibitions, removing market duties—all extend generous favor to benefit the people; only toward bandits and thieves they become still stricter and more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites list twelve famine policies—dispersing profit, lightening levies, easing punishments, employing labor, lifting prohibitions, removing market duties—all extending generous favor to help the people; only toward bandits and thieves does policy grow stricter.

sentences.zh: 蓋以饑饉之歲，盜賊必多，殘害良民，不可不除。

translations.literal: This is because in years of famine bandits and thieves are sure to multiply and harm good commoners—they cannot be left uneliminated.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years bandits multiply and harm good people—they cannot be left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 頃年嘗見州縣官吏，有不知治體，務為小仁。

translations.literal: In recent years your servant has seen prefectural and county officials who did not understand the substance of governance and strove for petty kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years I have seen prefectural and county officials who did not understand governance and strove for petty kindness.

sentences.zh: 遇凶年，劫盜斛斗，輒寬縱之，則盜賊公行，更相劫奪，鄉村大擾，不免廣有收捕，重加刑辟，或死或流，然後稍定。

translations.literal: When they met bad years and people robbed grain measures, they would leniently release them; then bandits walked openly, robbed one another in turn, villages were greatly disturbed, and inevitably there had to be widespread arrests, heavy additional punishments, some death and some exile—only then did things gradually settle.
translations.idiomatic: In bad years, when people robbed grain, they would leniently release them; then bandits operated openly, robbed one another, and villages were thrown into chaos. Inevitably there followed widespread arrests, harsh punishments, death and exile—only then did order gradually return.

sentences.zh: 今若朝廷明降敕文，豫言與減等斷放，是勸民為盜也。

translations.literal: If now the court clearly issues an edict beforehand announcing reduced sentencing and release, that is encouraging the people to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: If the court now issues an edict in advance announcing reduced sentences and release, that is encouraging people to become bandits.

sentences.zh: 百姓乏食，當輕徭薄賦、開倉振貸以救其死，不當使之自相劫奪。

translations.literal: When the hundred surnames lack food, one should lighten corvée and reduce levies, open granaries and extend relief loans to save them from death—not make them rob one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the people lack food, the state should lighten corvée, reduce levies, open granaries, and extend relief loans to save them—not leave them to rob one another.

sentences.zh: 今歲府界、京東、京西水災極多，嚴刑峻法以除盜賊，猶恐春冬之交，饑民嘯聚，不可禁禦，又况降敕以勸之。

translations.literal: This year the metropolitan region, Jingdong, and Jingxi have extremely many flood disasters; even with severe punishments and stern law to eliminate bandits, one still fears that at the turn of spring and winter hungry people will gather in uproar and cannot be restrained—how much more if an edict is issued to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: This year floods have struck the metropolitan region, Jingdong, and Jingxi on a vast scale. Even with severe punishments to suppress banditry, we still fear that at the turn of spring and winter hungry people may gather in unrest beyond control—how much more if an edict encourages them.

sentences.zh: 臣恐國家始於寬仁，而終於酷暴，意在活人而殺人更多也。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears the state will begin with lenient benevolence and end in cruel violence, intending to spare lives yet killing more people."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the state will begin with lenient benevolence and end in cruel violence—intending to spare lives yet killing more people."

sentences.zh: 事報聞。

translations.literal: The matter was reported and noted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was noted.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗御邇英閣經筵，講《周禮》「大荒大札，薄征緩刑 」，楊安國曰：「緩 刑者，乃過誤之民耳，當歲歉則赦之，憫其窮也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once attended the Classics lecture at the Erying Pavilion, where they expounded the Zhou Rites passage "great famine, great pestilence—lighten levies and ease punishments"; Yang Anguo said: "Easing punishments applies to people who erred through mistake; when the harvest fails one pardons them, pitying their destitution.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once attended a Classics lecture at the Erying Pavilion on the Zhou Rites passage "in great famine and great pestilence, lighten levies and ease punishments." Yang Anguo said, "Easing punishments applies to people who erred through mistake; when the harvest fails one pardons them out of pity for their destitution.

sentences.zh: 今眾持兵杖劫糧廩，一切寬之，恐不足以禁姦。」

translations.literal: Now when the multitude take up weapons and staffs to rob granaries, to pardon them all alike will probably not suffice to restrain wrongdoing."
translations.idiomatic: When crowds take up arms to raid granaries, to pardon them all alike will probably not suffice to restrain crime."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不然，天下皆吾赤子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That is not so—all under Heaven are my red infants.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is not so—all under Heaven are my children.

sentences.zh: 一遇饑饉，州縣不能振恤，饑莩所迫，遂至為盜，又捕而殺之，不亦甚乎？」

translations.literal: Once they meet famine, the prefectures and counties cannot relieve and succor them; driven by starving corpses along the roads, they come to be bandits—then to capture and kill them, is that not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: When famine strikes and prefectures and counties cannot relieve them, driven by hunger they turn to banditry—then to capture and kill them, is that not excessive?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗聽斷，尤以忠厚為主。

translations.literal: Renzong's hearings and decisions especially took loyal generosity as their foundation.
translations.idiomatic: In his hearings and decisions, Renzong especially prized loyal generosity.

sentences.zh: 隴安縣民誣平民五人為劫盜，尉悉執之，一人掠死，四人遂引服。

translations.literal: A commoner of Long'an county falsely accused five ordinary people of being bandits; the district captain arrested them all; one died under beating and the four then confessed.
translations.idiomatic: A man in Long'an county falsely accused five civilians of banditry. The district captain arrested them all; one died under torture and the other four confessed.

sentences.zh: 其家辨于州，州不為理，悉論死。

translations.literal: Their families appealed at the prefecture; the prefecture would not hear them and sentenced all to death.
translations.idiomatic: Their families appealed to the prefecture, which refused to hear them and sentenced all to death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，秦州捕得真盜，隴州吏當坐法而會赦，帝怒，特貶知州孫濟為雷州參軍，餘皆除名流嶺南。

translations.literal: Before long Qinzhou captured the real bandits; the Longzhou officials should have been punished by law but encountered an amnesty; the Emperor was angry and specially demoted Prefect Sun Ji to military aide of Leizhou; the rest were dismissed from office and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qinzhou captured the real bandits. The Longzhou officials should have been punished but encountered an amnesty. The Emperor was furious and demoted Prefect Sun Ji to military aide of Leizhou; the rest were dismissed and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 賜錢粟五家，復其役三年。

translations.literal: He bestowed money and grain on the five families and restored their corvée obligations for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed money and grain on the five families and exempted them from corvée for three years.

sentences.zh: 因下詔戒敕州縣。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict admonishing prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict admonishing prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 廣州司理參軍陳仲約誤入人死，有司當仲約公罪，應贖。

translations.literal: Chen Zhongyue, judicial aide of Guangzhou, by mistake caused a person's death; the authorities assessed Zhongyue with a public-service offense for which redemption was due.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongyue, judicial aide of Guangzhou, by mistake caused a death. The authorities assessed him with a public-service offense for which redemption was due.

sentences.zh: 帝謂審刑院張揆曰：「死者不可復生，而獄吏雖廢，復得敘官。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Zhang Kui of the Court for Review of Punishments: "The dead cannot live again, yet though a prison clerk is dismissed he can again be restored to office."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Zhang Kui of the Court for Review of Punishments, "The dead cannot live again, yet though a prison clerk is dismissed he can be restored to office."

sentences.zh: 命特治之，會赦勿敘用。

translations.literal: He ordered special punishment; if an amnesty came, he was not to be restored to employment.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered special punishment; even if an amnesty came, he was not to be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 尚書比部員外郎師仲說請老，自言恩得任子，帝以仲說嘗失入人死罪，不與。

translations.literal: Shizhong Shuo, outer-section vice director of the Ministry of Revenue's comparison bureau, requested retirement, saying that by grace he was entitled to appoint a son to office; the Emperor, because Shuo had once by mistake entered a person into a capital offense, did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong Shuo of the Ministry of Revenue requested retirement, claiming entitlement by grace to appoint a son to office. The Emperor refused, because Shuo had once by mistake entered a person into a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 其重人命如此。

translations.literal: This is how greatly he valued human life.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his regard for human life.

sentences.zh: 時近臣有罪，多不下吏劾實，不付有司議法。

translations.literal: At the time when nearby ministers committed offenses, they were mostly not sent down to clerks for investigation of facts and were not handed to the authorities to deliberate on law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, when court favorites committed offenses, they were rarely sent to clerks for investigation or handed to the legal authorities for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 諫官王贄言：「情有輕重，理分故失，而一切出於聖斷，前後差異，有傷政體，刑法之官安所用哉？

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Wang Zhi said: "Circumstances have severity and leniency; principle distinguishes intent and negligence—yet if everything comes from the sage's decision with differences before and after, the substance of governance is harmed—of what use are the officials of penal law?
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Wang Zhi said, "Circumstances vary in severity; principle distinguishes intent from negligence—yet if everything is decided by imperial fiat with inconsistent results, governance is harmed. Of what use are the penal officials?

sentences.zh: 請自今悉付有司正以法。」

translations.literal: Request that from now on all be handed entirely to the authorities to judge correctly by law."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on all such cases be handed to the legal authorities for judgment according to law."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 近臣間有干請，輒為言官所斥。

translations.literal: When nearby ministers occasionally made personal requests, they were at once rebuked by remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: When court favorites made personal requests, remonstrance officials rebuked them at once.

sentences.zh: 諫官陳升之嘗言：「有司斷獄，或事連權倖，多以中旨釋之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Chen Shengzhi once said: "When the authorities decide cases, sometimes matters involve powerful favorites and are mostly released on inner edict.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Chen Shengzhi once said, "When the authorities decide cases involving powerful favorites, they are often released on secret imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 請有緣中旨得釋者，劾其干請之罪，以違制論。」

translations.literal: Request that those released because of inner edict be impeached for the crime of personal request, judged as violation of regulations."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that those released by such orders be impeached for improper solicitation, judged as violation of regulations."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 仁宗於賞罰無所私，尤不以貴近廢法。

translations.literal: Renzong in rewards and punishments showed no partiality and especially did not set aside law because of noble proximity.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong showed no partiality in rewards and punishments and especially would not set aside law for the well connected.

sentences.zh: 屢戒有司：「被內降者，執奏，毋輒行。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly admonished the authorities: "When you receive an inner descent, hold it and memorialize—do not carry it out at once."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly admonished officials, "When you receive a secret imperial order, memorialize and hold it—do not carry it out at once."

sentences.zh: 未嘗屈法以自徇也。

translations.literal: He never bent law to indulge himself.
translations.idiomatic: He never bent the law to indulge himself.

sentences.zh: 知虢州周日宣詭奏水災，有司論請如上書不實法。

translations.literal: Zhou Rixuan, prefect of Guozhou, falsely memorialized a flood disaster; the authorities deliberated and requested sentencing under the statute for untrue memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Rixuan, prefect of Guozhou, falsely reported a flood. The authorities proposed sentencing under the statute for untrue memorials.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「州郡多言符瑞，至水旱之災，或抑而不聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Prefectures and commanderies speak much of omens and portents, yet when it comes to flood and drought disasters they sometimes suppress them and do not report.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Prefectures report omens readily enough, yet when floods and droughts strike they sometimes suppress the news.

sentences.zh: 今守臣自陳墊溺官私廬舍，意實在民，何可加罪？」

translations.literal: Now the guarding minister himself reports inundation of official and private dwellings—his intent is truly for the people—how can punishment be added?"
translations.idiomatic: Now this prefect reports inundation of official and private dwellings himself—his intent is truly for the people. How can we punish him?"

sentences.zh: 英宗在位日淺，於政令未及有所更制。

translations.literal: Yingzong's days on the throne were short; he had not yet been able to reform governmental orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong reigned briefly and had not yet been able to reform governmental orders.

sentences.zh: 然以吏習平安，慢於奉法，稍欲振起其怠惰。

translations.literal: Yet because officials were accustomed to peace and security and were slack in upholding law, he slightly wished to rouse their indolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because officials had grown accustomed to peace and were slack in upholding law, he wished slightly to rouse their indolence.

sentences.zh: 三班奉職和欽貸所部綱錢，至絞，帝命貸死免杖，刺隸福建路牢城。

translations.literal: He Qin, a third-rank attendant on duty, lent out his unit's transport funds and faced strangulation; the Emperor ordered commutation of death and exemption from beating, tattooing and registering him in a Fujian circuit penal fortress.
translations.idiomatic: He Qin, a third-rank attendant, had lent out his unit's transport funds and faced strangulation. The Emperor commuted death and exempted beating, branding him and registering him in a Fujian penal fortress.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院盧士宗請稍寬其罪，帝曰：「 刑故而得寬，則死者滋眾 ，非『刑期無刑』之道。

translations.literal: Lu Shizong, director of the Court for Review of Punishments, requested slightly to lighten his offense; the Emperor said: "When intentional crimes receive leniency, those who die multiply—it is not the Way of 'punishment aims at no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shizong, director of the Court for Review of Punishments, asked to lighten the sentence. The Emperor said, "When intentional crimes receive leniency, executions multiply—that is not the Way of 'punishment aims at no punishment.

sentences.zh: 俟有過誤，貸無傷也。」

translations.literal: Wait until there is error through negligence—then commutation does no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Wait until there is negligence through mistake—then commutation does no harm."

sentences.zh: 富國倉監官受米濕惡，壞十八萬石，會恩當減，帝特命奪官停之。

translations.literal: The supervisor of the Fuguo granary accepted damp and spoiled grain and ruined one hundred eighty thousand piculs; an amnesty would have reduced the sentence; the Emperor specially ordered removal from office and suspension.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor of the Fuguo granary accepted damp, spoiled grain and ruined 180,000 piculs. An amnesty would have reduced the sentence, but the Emperor specially ordered removal from office and suspension.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，內殿崇班鄭從易母、兄俱亡於嶺外，歲餘方知，請行服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Zheng Congyi of the Inner Hall Honored Class—both his mother and elder brother had died beyond the ranges and only after more than a year did he learn of it—requested to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 2, Zheng Congyi of the Inner Hall Honored Class learned only after more than a year that his mother and elder brother had both died in the far south and requested mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「父母在遠，當朝夕為念。

translations.literal: Shenzong said: "When parents are far away, one should think of them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong said, "When parents are far away, one should think of them morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 經時無安否之問，以至踰年不知存亡邪？」

translations.literal: To go so long without asking whether they are safe or ill, until more than a year passes without knowing whether they live or die—is that permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: To go so long without asking after their welfare, until more than a year passes without knowing whether they live or die—is that permissible?"

sentences.zh: 特除名勒停。

translations.literal: He was specially struck from the rolls and suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls and suspended.

sentences.zh: 四年，王存立言：「嘉祐中，同學究出身，為碭山縣尉，嘗納官贖父配隸罪，請同舉人法，得免丁徭。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Wang Cunli spoke: "In the Jiayou era, having passed the same examination for classicist origin, I served as district captain of Dangshan county and once paid the authorities to redeem my father's offense of penal registration—request that under the same rule as examination graduates I may be exempted from corvée and levies."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Wang Cunli memorialized, "In the Jiayou era, having passed the examination for classicist origin, I served as district captain of Dangshan and once paid the authorities to redeem my father's offense of penal registration. I ask that, like examination graduates, I be exempted from corvée and levies."

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，復賜出身，仍與注官。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied him, restored his examination origin, and still granted him an office appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took pity on him, restored his examination status, and still granted him an office appointment.

sentences.zh: 九年，知桂州沈起欲經略交趾，取其慈恩州，交人遂破欽，犯邕管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shen Qi, prefect of Guizhou, wished to pacify Jiaozhi and seize its Ci'en prefecture; the Jiao people then broke Qin and invaded Yong and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Shen Qi, prefect of Guizhou, sought to pacify Jiaozhi and seize Ci'en prefecture. The Jiao people then overran Qin and invaded Yong and Guan.

sentences.zh: 詔邊人橫遭屠戮，職其致寇，罪悉在起，特削官爵，編置遠惡州。

translations.literal: An edict said the border people had suffered slaughter in vain—the blame for bringing the invaders lay with Qi; all guilt was on Qi; he was specially stripped of office and rank and registered in a distant, harsh prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that border people had been slaughtered in vain and that Qi alone was responsible for bringing the invaders. He was stripped of office and rank and registered in a distant, harsh prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復讎，後世無法。

translations.literal: Blood vengeance—later ages have no law for it.
translations.idiomatic: Blood vengeance had no place in later law.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時，單州民劉玉父為王德毆死，德更赦，玉私殺德以復父讎。

translations.literal: In Renzong's time, Liu Yu of Shanzhou—his father had been beaten to death by Wang De; De later received amnesty; Yu privately killed De to avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong, Liu Yu of Shanzhou—his father had been beaten to death by Wang De. After De received amnesty, Yu privately killed him to avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 帝義之， 杖、編管。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his conduct morally; he was beaten and placed under registered supervision.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his conduct morally; he was beaten and placed under registered supervision.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年，青州民王贇父為人毆死，贇幼，未能復讎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng, Wang Yun of Qingzhou—his father had been beaten to death by another; Yun was young and could not yet take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 1, Wang Yun of Qingzhou—his father had been beaten to death by another. Yun was young and could not yet take revenge.

sentences.zh: 幾冠，刺讎，斷支首祭父墓，自首，論當斬，帝以殺讎祭父，又自歸罪，其情可矜，詔貸死，刺配鄰州。

translations.literal: When he was nearly capped, he stabbed his enemy, cut off a limb and head to sacrifice at his father's tomb, and surrendered himself; by law he should be beheaded; the Emperor, because he had killed his enemy to sacrifice to his father and also surrendered himself, found his circumstances pitiable, ordered commutation of death, and tattooed and assigned him to a neighboring prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nearly of age, he stabbed his enemy, cut off a limb and head to sacrifice at his father's tomb, and surrendered. By law he faced execution, but the Emperor found his circumstances pitiable—he had killed his enemy to honor his father and had surrendered himself—and commuted death, branding him and assigning him to a neighboring prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣州民葉元，有同居兄亂其妻，縊殺之，又殺兄子，強其父與嫂為約契不訟。

translations.literal: Ye Yuan, a commoner of Xuanzhou, had a coresident elder brother who violated his wife; he strangled and killed the brother, also killed the brother's son, and forced his father and sister-in-law to make a written pact not to sue.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yuan of Xuanzhou had a coresident elder brother who violated his wife. He strangled the brother, killed the brother's son, and forced his father and sister-in-law to sign a pact not to sue.

sentences.zh: 鄰里發其事，州為上請，帝曰：「罪人以死，姦亂之事特出葉元之口，不足以定罪。

translations.literal: Neighbors exposed the matter; the prefecture memorialized upward; the Emperor said: "To punish a person with death—the affair of adultery and disorder comes solely from Ye Yuan's mouth and is insufficient to establish guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors exposed the matter and the prefecture memorialized upward. The Emperor said, "To punish with death—the charge of adultery and disorder rests solely on Ye Yuan's word and is insufficient to convict.

sentences.zh: 且下民雖無知，固宜哀矜，然以妻子之愛，既罔其父，又殺其兄，戕其姪，逆理敗倫，宜以毆兄至死律論。」

translations.literal: Moreover, though common people below are ignorant and should indeed be pitied, yet for love of wife and children he deceived his father, also killed his elder brother, and destroyed his nephew—against principle and ruining human relations—he should be judged under the statute for beating an elder brother to death."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though common people deserve pity, for love of his wife he deceived his father, killed his elder brother, and destroyed his nephew—against principle and ruining human relations. He should be judged under the statute for beating an elder brother to death."

sentences.zh: 紹聖以來，連起黨獄，忠良屏斥，國以空虛。

translations.literal: From Shaosheng onward, factional prosecutions arose in succession; loyal and good men were excluded; the state grew hollow.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shaosheng era onward, factional prosecutions arose in succession, loyal officials were driven out, and the state grew hollow.

sentences.zh: 徽宗嗣位，外事耳目之玩，內窮聲色之欲，徵發亡度，號令靡常。

translations.literal: Huizong succeeded to the throne; outwardly he pursued diversions for eye and ear, inwardly he exhausted himself in sound and beauty; levies and conscription knew no measure; orders and commands were inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong succeeded, he pursued outward diversions and inward indulgence in pleasure, levied without measure, and issued inconstant orders.

sentences.zh: 於是蔡京、王黼之屬，得以誣上行私，變亂法制。

translations.literal: Thereupon men like Cai Jing and Wang Fu were able to deceive the ruler and pursue private ends, transforming and disordering statutes and institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon men like Cai Jing and Wang Fu were able to deceive the ruler, pursue private ends, and overturn statutes and institutions.

sentences.zh: 崇寧五年，詔曰：「出令制法，重輕予奪在上。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning, an edict said: "Issuing orders and making law—the weighting of severity and leniency, granting and taking away, lies with the ruler above.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning 5, an edict said, "Issuing orders and making law—the weighting of severity and leniency, granting and taking away, lies with the ruler.

sentences.zh: 比降特旨處分，而三省引用敕令，以為妨礙，沮抑不行，是以有司之常守，格人主之威福。

translations.literal: Recently special edicts have been issued for disposition, yet the Three Departments cite ordinances as obstructing and block execution—thus the regular duties of officials check the sovereign's authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Recently special edicts have been issued, yet the Three Departments cite ordinances as obstructing them and block execution—thus routine official duties check the sovereign's authority.

sentences.zh: 夫擅殺生之謂王，能利害之謂王，何格令之有？

translations.literal: To monopolize life and death is called kingship; to be able to benefit and harm is called kingship—what need is there for regulations and ordinances?
translations.idiomatic: To monopolize life and death is kingship; to benefit and harm at will is kingship—what need for regulations and ordinances?

sentences.zh: 臣強之漸，不可不戒。

translations.literal: The gradual advance of ministerial strength cannot go unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: The gradual advance of ministerial power cannot go unheeded.

sentences.zh: 自今應有特旨處分，間有利害，明具論奏，虛心以聽；

translations.literal: From now on, whenever there are special edict dispositions, if there are pros and cons, clearly set them forth in memorial and listen with an open mind;
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever special edict dispositions arise, if there are pros and cons, set them forth clearly in memorial and listen with an open mind;

sentences.zh: 如或以常法沮格不行，以大不恭論。」

translations.literal: if anyone blocks execution with regular law, judge it as great irreverence."
translations.idiomatic: if anyone blocks execution with regular law, judge it as great irreverence."

sentences.zh: 明年，詔：「凡御筆斷罪，不許詣尚書省陳訴。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict: "For all crimes decided by imperial brush, appeal to the Department of State Affairs is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, an edict declared, "For all crimes decided by imperial brush, appeal to the Department of State Affairs is not permitted.

sentences.zh: 如違，並以違御筆論。」

translations.literal: If violated, all are judged as violating the imperial brush."
translations.idiomatic: Violators are judged as violating the imperial brush."

sentences.zh: 又定令：「凡應承受御筆官府，稽滯一時杖一百，一日徒二年，二日加一等，罪止流三千里，三日以大不恭論。」

translations.literal: Regulations were also fixed: "For all offices that should receive the imperial brush, delay of one period—one hundred blows with the rod; one day—two years' penal servitude; two days—one grade added; maximum offense exile three thousand li; three days—great irreverence."
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were also fixed: "For offices that should receive the imperial brush, delay of one period—one hundred blows; one day—two years' penal servitude; two days—one grade added; maximum offense—exile three thousand li; three days—great irreverence."

sentences.zh: 由是吏因緣為姦，用法巧文寖深，無復祖宗忠厚之志。

translations.literal: Thereby clerks seized opportunities for corruption; applying law with crafty wording grew ever deeper, and there was no longer the ancestors' spirit of loyal generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby clerks seized opportunities for corruption; legal craft grew ever harsher, and the ancestors' spirit of loyal generosity was lost.

sentences.zh: 窮極奢侈，以竭民力，自速禍機。

translations.literal: Extravagance was pushed to the limit, exhausting the people's strength and hastening calamity by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance was pushed to the limit, the people's strength was exhausted, and they hastened calamity themselves.

sentences.zh: 靖康雖知悔悟，稍誅姦惡，而謀國匪人，終亦末如之何矣。

translations.literal: At Jingkang they knew repentance, slightly executed treacherous evildoers, yet those who schemed against the state were unworthy men—in the end nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang they knew repentance and executed some traitors, yet unworthy men still schemed against the state—in the end nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 高宗性仁柔，其於用法，每從寬厚，罪有過貸，而未嘗過殺。

translations.literal: Gaozong's nature was benevolent and gentle; in applying law he always followed lenient generosity—when offenses allowed commutation he commuted, and he never over-killed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was benevolent and gentle; in applying law he always favored leniency—commuting when possible and never over-punishing with death.

sentences.zh: 知常州周擅殺人，帝曰：「朕日親聽斷，豈不能任情誅僇，顧非理耳。」

translations.literal: Zhou, prefect of Changzhou, killed a person on his own authority; the Emperor said: "I daily hear cases in person—could I not punish as I please? I only look to what is not reasonable."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, prefect of Changzhou, killed someone on his own authority. The Emperor said, "I hear cases daily in person—could I not punish as I please? I look only to what is unreasonable."

sentences.zh: 即命削籍。

translations.literal: He at once ordered him struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered him struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 大理率以儒臣用法平允者為之。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review generally appointed Confucian officials who applied law fairly.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review generally appointed Confucian officials who applied law fairly.

sentences.zh: 獄官入對，即以慘酷為戒。

translations.literal: When prison officials entered audience, he immediately admonished them against cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: When prison officials entered audience, he admonished them against cruelty.

sentences.zh: 臺臣、士曹有所平反，輒與之轉官。

translations.literal: Whenever censorate officials or judicial clerks reversed wrongful convictions, he at once promoted them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever censors or judicial clerks reversed wrongful convictions, he promoted them at once.

sentences.zh: 每臨軒慮囚，未嘗有送下者，曰：「吾恐有司觀望，鍛鍊以為重輕也。」

translations.literal: Each time he faced the hall to review prisoners, there was never one sent back down; he said: "I fear the authorities will watch and wait, forging cases to make severity or leniency."
translations.idiomatic: Each time he reviewed prisoners in court, none were sent back down. He said, "I fear officials will watch and wait, forging cases to adjust severity."

sentences.zh: 吏部員外郎劉大中奉使江南回，遷左司諫，帝尋以為祕書少監。

translations.literal: Liu Dazhong, outer-section vice director of the Ministry of Personnel, returned from a mission to Jiangnan and was transferred to Left Bureau remonstrance official; the Emperor soon made him vice director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dazhong of the Ministry of Personnel returned from a mission to Jiangnan and was made Left Bureau remonstrance official; the Emperor soon appointed him vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 謂宰臣朱勝非曰：「大中奉使，頗多興獄，今使為諫官，恐四方觀望耳。」

translations.literal: He said to chief minister Zhu Shengfei: "On his mission Dazhong raised many prosecutions; now to make him a remonstrance official—I fear the four directions will take it as a signal."
translations.idiomatic: He told chief minister Zhu Shengfei, "On his mission Dazhong raised many prosecutions; to make him a remonstrance official now—I fear the realm will take it as a signal."

sentences.zh: 其用心忠厚如此。

translations.literal: His loyal generosity of mind was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his loyal generosity of mind.

sentences.zh: 後詔：「用刑慘酷責降之人，勿堂除及親民，止與遠小監當差遣。」

translations.literal: Later an edict: "Those demoted for cruel use of punishment are not to receive hall appointments or posts among the people—only distant minor supervisory assignments."
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict declared, "Those demoted for cruel punishment are not to receive hall appointments or posts among the people—only distant minor supervisory assignments."

sentences.zh: 當建、紹間，天下盜起，往往攻城屠邑，至興師以討之，然得貸亦眾。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan and Shaoxing era, bandits arose throughout the realm, often storming cities and slaughtering towns, until armies were raised to suppress them—yet many also received commutation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan and Shaoxing era, bandits arose throughout the realm, storming cities and slaughtering towns until armies were raised to suppress them—yet many also received commutation.

sentences.zh: 同知樞密院事李回嘗奏強盜之數，帝曰：「皆吾赤子也，豈可一一誅之？

translations.literal: Vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Hui once memorialized the number of armed robbers; the Emperor said: "They are all my red infants—how can they be executed one by one?
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Li Hui once reported the number of armed robbers. The Emperor said, "They are all my children—how can they be executed one by one?

sentences.zh: 誅其渠魁三兩人足矣。」

translations.literal: Executing two or three ringleaders is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Executing two or three ringleaders is enough."

sentences.zh: 至待貪吏則極嚴：應受贓者，不許堂除及親民；

translations.literal: Toward corrupt officials he was extremely strict: those who should receive bribes were not permitted hall appointments or posts among the people;
translations.idiomatic: Toward corrupt officials he was extremely strict: those who took bribes were barred from hall appointments and posts among the people;

sentences.zh: 犯枉法自盜者，籍其名中書，罪至徒即不敘，至死者，籍其貲。

translations.literal: those who violated law by self-theft had their names registered at the Secretariat; if the offense reached penal servitude they were not restored; if it reached death, their property was registered.
translations.idiomatic: those who violated law by embezzlement had their names registered at the Secretariat; if the offense reached penal servitude they were not restored; if it reached death, their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 諸文臣寄祿官並帶「左」、「右」字，贓罪人則去之。

translations.literal: All civil officials on salary appointments bore the characters "Left" or "Right"; corrupt offenders had them removed.
translations.idiomatic: All civil officials on salary appointments bore the characters "Left" or "Right"; corrupt offenders had them removed.

sentences.zh: 是年，申嚴真決贓吏法。

translations.literal: That year, the law for truly executing corrupt officials was strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the law for truly executing corrupt officials was strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 令三省取具祖宗故事，有以舊法棄市事上者，帝曰：「何至爾耶？

translations.literal: He ordered the Three Departments to gather ancestral precedents; when someone memorialized an old-law case of marketplace execution, the Emperor said: "How could it go that far?
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Three Departments to gather ancestral precedents. When someone memorialized an old-law case of marketplace execution, the Emperor said, "How could it go that far?

sentences.zh: 但斷遣之足矣。

translations.literal: Simply sentencing and dispatching them is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Simply sentencing and dispatching them is enough.

sentences.zh: 貪吏害民，雜用刑威，有不得已，然豈忍寘縉紳於死地邪？」

translations.literal: Corrupt officials harm the people; mixed use of penal authority is sometimes unavoidable—yet how could one bear to place gentry-officials in the place of death?"
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials harm the people; harsh punishment is sometimes unavoidable—yet how could one bear to put gentry-officials to death?"

sentences.zh: 在徽宗時，刑法已峻，雖嘗裁定笞杖之制，而有司猶從重比。

translations.literal: Under Huizong, penal law was already severe; although the rod-and-cudgel system was once fixed, the authorities still followed heavy analogies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Huizong, penal law was already severe; although the rod-and-cudgel system was once fixed, officials still followed heavy analogies.

sentences.zh: 中興之初，詔用政和遞減法，自是迄嘉定不易。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the restoration, an edict ordered use of the Zhenghe progressive-reduction method; from then until Jiading it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the restoration, an edict ordered use of the Zhenghe progressive-reduction method; from then until Jiading it was not changed.

sentences.zh: 自蔡京當國，凡所請御筆以壞正法者，悉釐正之。

translations.literal: From the time Cai Jing held the state, all imperial-brush requests that had damaged correct law were entirely rectified.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Cai Jing held power, all imperial-brush measures that had damaged correct law were rectified.

sentences.zh: 諸獄具，令當職官依式檢校。

translations.literal: For all prison implements, duty officers were ordered to inspect according to the formulary.
translations.idiomatic: For all prison implements, duty officers were ordered to inspect according to the formulary.

sentences.zh: 枷以乾木為之，輕重長短刻識其上，笞杖不得留節目，亦不得釘飾及加筋膠之類，仍用官給火印。

translations.literal: Cangues were made of dry wood; weight, lightness, length, and shortness were carved and marked on them; beating rods were not to retain nodes, nor be nailed, decorated, or reinforced with sinew and glue; official fire seals were still used.
translations.idiomatic: Cangues were made of dry wood with weight and dimensions marked on them. Beating rods were not to retain nodes or be reinforced or decorated. Official fire seals were still required.

sentences.zh: 暑月每五日一洗濯枷杻，刑、寺輪官一員，躬親監視。

translations.literal: In summer months cangues and fetters were washed every five days; the Penal and Judicial offices rotated one officer to supervise in person.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, cangues and fetters were washed every five days, with one officer from the Penal and Judicial offices rotating to supervise in person.

sentences.zh: 諸獄司並旬申禁狀，品官、命婦在禁，別具單狀。

translations.literal: All prison offices reported detention status every ten days; ranked officials and titled ladies in detention had separate single reports.
translations.idiomatic: All prison offices reported detention status every ten days; ranked officials and titled ladies in detention had separate reports.

sentences.zh: 合奏案者，具情款招伏奏聞，法司朱書檢坐條例、推司錄問、檢法官吏姓名于後。

translations.literal: Cases requiring memorial had the facts and confessions set forth and memorialized; the legal office wrote in vermilion the cited statutes, the investigating office's recorded interrogation, and the names of examining officials at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Cases requiring memorial set forth the facts and confessions; the legal office wrote in vermilion the cited statutes, the investigating office's interrogation record, and the names of examining officials at the end.

sentences.zh: 各州每年開收編配羈管奴婢人及斷過編配之數，各置籍。

translations.literal: Each prefecture annually opened and closed registers of persons assigned, registered, or detained under restraint, and slaves, and the numbers sentenced to assignment—each kept its own register.
translations.idiomatic: Each prefecture annually registered persons assigned, registered, detained under restraint, and slaves, and kept registers of sentences to assignment.

sentences.zh: 各路提點刑獄司，歲具本路州軍斷過大辟申刑部，諸州申提刑司。

translations.literal: Each circuit's judicial-intendant office annually compiled capital sentences in the circuit's prefectures and armies and reported to the Ministry of Justice; prefectures reported to the judicial-intendant office.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit's judicial-intendant office annually reported capital sentences in its prefectures to the Ministry of Justice; prefectures reported to the judicial-intendant office.

sentences.zh: 其應書禁曆而不書，應申所屬而不申，奏案不依式，檢坐開具違令，回報不圓致妨詳覆，與提刑司詳覆大辟而稽留、失覆大辟致罪有出入者，各抵罪。

translations.literal: Those who should record the detention calendar but did not, should report to superiors but did not, memorialized cases not according to form, cited and listed violations of orders, replies incomplete causing obstruction of detailed review, or who with the judicial-intendant office reviewed capital cases but delayed, or failed to review capital cases causing discrepancy in guilt—all faced punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed to record detention calendars, failed to report upward, memorialized cases not according to form, cited statutes incorrectly, gave incomplete replies obstructing review, delayed capital review with the judicial-intendant office, or failed to review capital cases causing sentencing errors—all faced punishment.

sentences.zh: 知州兼統兵者，非出師臨陳，毋用重刑。

translations.literal: Prefects who also commanded troops were not to use heavy punishments unless deploying armies to face battle.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects who also commanded troops were not to use heavy punishments unless deploying armies to battle.

sentences.zh: 州縣月具繫囚存亡之數申提刑司，歲終比較，死囚最多者，當職官黜責，其最少者，褒賞之。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties monthly reported numbers of prisoners held and surviving to the judicial-intendant office; at year-end comparisons were made—where dead prisoners were most numerous, duty officers were demoted and blamed; where least, rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties monthly reported prisoner numbers to the judicial-intendant office. At year-end, officials in districts with the most deaths in custody were demoted; those with the fewest were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 舊以絹計贓者，千三百為一匹，竊盜至二貫者徒 。

translations.literal: Formerly when calculating stolen goods in silk, thirteen hundred counted as one bolt; theft reaching two strings brought penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when calculating stolen goods in silk, 1,300 cash counted as one bolt; theft reaching two strings brought penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 至是，又加優減，以二千為一匹，盜至三貫者徒一年。

translations.literal: At this time further lenient reduction was added: two thousand for one bolt; theft reaching three strings brought one year penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Now further lenient reduction was added: 2,000 for one bolt; theft reaching three strings brought one year penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 三年 ，復詔以三千為一匹，竊盜及凡以錢定罪，遞增五分。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict again set three thousand for one bolt; for theft and all offenses judged by cash, increase by five parts in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict set 3,000 for one bolt; for theft and all cash-based offenses, thresholds increased by five parts in succession.

sentences.zh: 四年，又詔：「特旨處死，情法不當者，許大理寺奏審。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, another edict: "When special edicts order death but sentiment and law are inappropriate, the Court of Judicial Review may memorialize for review."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, another edict declared, "When special edicts order death but circumstances and law do not warrant it, the Court of Judicial Review may memorialize for review."

sentences.zh: 五年，歲終比較，宣州、衢州、福州無病死囚，當職官各轉一官；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, year-end comparison: Xuanzhou, Quzhou, and Fuzhou had no prisoners who died of illness in custody; duty officers each advanced one rank;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, year-end comparison showed Xuanzhou, Quzhou, and Fuzhou had no prisoners who died of illness in custody; duty officers each advanced one rank;

sentences.zh: 舒州病死及一分，惠州二分六釐，當職官各降一官。

translations.literal: Shuzhou illness deaths reached one part in ten; Huizhou two parts six tenths in a hundred; duty officers each were reduced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhou had illness deaths reaching one in ten; Huizhou two and six tenths in a hundred; duty officers each were reduced one rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，令刑部體量公事，邵州、廣州、高州勘命官淹係至久不報，詔知州降一官，當職官展二年磨勘，當行吏永不收敘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Justice was ordered to assess public business; Shaozhou, Guangzhou, and Gaozhou investigating officials detained persons for extremely long periods without reporting; an edict reduced prefects one rank, extended duty officers' merit review two years, and clerks who handled cases were never restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Justice was ordered to assess cases. Shaozhou, Guangzhou, and Gaozhou kept detainees for extremely long periods without reporting. Prefects were reduced one rank, duty officers' merit review was extended two years, and handling clerks were never restored.

sentences.zh: 德慶府勘封川縣令事，七月不報，詔知州、勘官各抵罪。

translations.literal: Deqing prefecture investigated the Fengchuan county magistrate's case and did not report for seven months; an edict ordered the prefect and investigating officials each to face punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Deqing investigated a Fengchuan county magistrate's case and did not report for seven months. The prefect and investigating officials each faced punishment.

sentences.zh: 九年，大理寺朱伯文廣西催斷刑獄，還言：「雷州海賊兩獄，並係平人七人，內五人已死。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Zhu Bowen of the Court of Judicial Review hurried to conclude cases in Guangxi and on returning said: "Two cases of Leizhou sea bandits both involved seven ordinary people; within, five were already dead."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, Zhu Bowen of the Court of Judicial Review hurried to conclude cases in Guangxi and reported, "Two Leizhou sea-bandit cases both involved seven ordinary people; five were already dead."

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，詔本路提刑以下重致罰。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved to pity and ordered heavy punishment for the circuit judicial intendant and below.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved to pity and ordered heavy punishment for the circuit judicial intendant and below.

sentences.zh: 十二年，御史臺點檢錢塘、仁和縣獄具，錢塘大杖，一多五錢半；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Censorate inspected prison implements of Qiantang and Renhe counties; Qiantang's heavy rods—one was five and a half cash too heavy;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Censorate inspected prison implements in Qiantang and Renhe counties. One Qiantang heavy rod was five and a half cash too heavy;

sentences.zh: 仁和枷，一多一斤，一輕半斤。

translations.literal: Renhe cangues—one was one jin too heavy, one half a jin too light.
translations.idiomatic: one Renhe cangue was one jin too heavy, another half a jin too light.

sentences.zh: 詔縣官各降一官。

translations.literal: An edict reduced county officials each one rank.
translations.idiomatic: County officials were each reduced one rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔：「禁囚無供飯者，臨安日支錢二十文，外路十五文。」

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict: "Detained prisoners without provided meals—at Lin'an twenty cash per day, on outer circuits fifteen cash."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, an edict declared, "Detained prisoners without provided meals receive twenty cash per day at Lin'an and fifteen on outer circuits."

sentences.zh: 十六年，詔：「諸鞫獄追到干證人，無罪遣還者，每程給米一升半，錢十五文。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict: "For all interrogations that summon key witnesses, when innocents are sent back, each stage of journey gives one and a half sheng of rice and fifteen cash."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, an edict declared, "When key witnesses summoned for interrogation are found innocent and sent home, each stage of journey provides one and a half sheng of rice and fifteen cash."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，詔官支病囚藥物錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, an edict ordered official payment for sick prisoners' medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, an edict ordered official payment for sick prisoners' medicine.

sentences.zh: 舊法，刑部郎官四人，分左右廳，或以詳覆，或以敘雪 ，同僚而異事，有防閑考覆之意。

translations.literal: Under old law, four Ministry of Justice bureau directors divided into left and right halls—some for detailed review, some for petitioning redress—colleagues with different duties, having the intent of mutual checks and review.
translations.idiomatic: Under old law, four Ministry of Justice bureau directors divided into left and right halls—some for detailed review, some for petitioning redress—colleagues with different duties for mutual checks.

sentences.zh: 南渡以來，務從簡省，大理少卿止一員，刑部郎中初無分異，獄有不得其情，法有不當於理者，無所平反追改。

translations.literal: Since the crossing south, striving for simplification, the Court of Judicial Review had only one vice director; Ministry of Justice directors initially had no division—when cases did not obtain the facts, when law did not accord with reason, there was nowhere to reverse and amend.
translations.idiomatic: Since the crossing south, striving for simplification, the Court of Judicial Review had only one vice director and Ministry of Justice directors had no division—when cases missed the facts or law missed reason, there was no mechanism to reverse and amend.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，右司郎中汪應辰言之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Wang Yingchen, director of the Right Bureau, spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, Wang Yingchen of the Right Bureau spoke of this.

sentences.zh: 詔刑部郎官依元豐法，分左右廳治事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ministry of Justice directors to follow Yuanfeng law and divide into left and right halls to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Ministry of Justice directors to follow Yuanfeng law and divide into left and right halls.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，詔：「四川以錢引科罪者，準銅錢。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, an edict: "In Sichuan, offenses judged by paper money notes are equated to copper cash."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, an edict declared, "In Sichuan, offenses judged by paper money notes are equated to copper cash."

sentences.zh: 孝宗究心庶獄，每歲臨軒慮囚，率先數日令有司進款案披閱，然後決遣。

translations.literal: Xiaozong devoted his mind to ordinary cases; each year when he faced the hall to review prisoners, several days beforehand he ordered the authorities to submit case records for perusal, then decided and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong devoted himself to ordinary cases. Each year before reviewing prisoners in court, he ordered authorities to submit case records several days in advance for perusal, then decided and dispatched.

sentences.zh: 法司更定律令，必親為訂正之。

translations.literal: When the legal office revised statutes and ordinances, he always personally corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: When the legal office revised statutes and ordinances, he always corrected them personally.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙雄上《淳熙條法事類》，帝讀至收騾馬、舟舡、契書稅，曰：「恐後世有算及舟車之譏。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhao Xiong submitted the Chunxi Classified Statutes; when the Emperor read as far as taxes on mules, horses, boats, ships, and contracts, he said: "I fear later ages will have the reproach of counting boats and carts."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhao Xiong submitted the Chunxi Classified Statutes. When the Emperor read taxes on mules, horses, boats, ships, and contracts, he said, "I fear later ages will reproach us for taxing boats and carts."

sentences.zh: 《戶令》：「戶絕之家，許給其家三千貫，及二萬貫者取旨。」

translations.literal: The Household Ordinance: "For households extinct in the male line, permit giving the family three thousand strings; for twenty thousand strings, obtain imperial instruction."
translations.idiomatic: The Household Ordinance read, "For extinct households, permit giving the family three thousand strings; for twenty thousand strings, obtain imperial instruction."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「其家不幸而絕，及二萬貫迺取之，是有心利其財也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Their family unfortunately became extinct—only at twenty thousand strings do we take it; this shows intent to profit from their property."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Their family unfortunately became extinct—only at twenty thousand strings do we take it. That shows intent to profit from their property."

sentences.zh: 又《捕亡律》：「公人不獲盜者，罰金。」

translations.literal: Again the Arrest of Fugitives statute: "When government agents do not capture bandits, fine them."
translations.idiomatic: Again the Arrest of Fugitives statute read, "When government agents fail to capture bandits, fine them."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「罰金而不加罪，是使之受財縱盜也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "To fine without adding guilt is to make them take money and release bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "To fine without adding guilt is to let them take money and release bandits."

sentences.zh: 又：「監司、知州無額上供者賞。」

translations.literal: Again: "Circuit intendants and prefects who supply tribute beyond quota are rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: Again: "Circuit intendants and prefects who supply tribute beyond quota are rewarded."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「上供既無額，是白取於民也，可賞以誘之乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Since tribute has no quota, this is taking openly from the people—can we reward to entice it?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Since tribute has no quota, this is taking openly from the people—can we reward it to encourage more?"

sentences.zh: 並令削去之。

translations.literal: He ordered all struck out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered all struck out.

sentences.zh: 其明審如此。

translations.literal: His clarity and scrutiny were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his clarity and scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 且於用刑 ，未嘗以私廢法。

translations.literal: Moreover in applying punishment, he never set aside law for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in applying punishment he never set aside law for private ends.

sentences.zh: 鎮江都統戚方以刻剝被罪，宰臣陳俊卿言內臣有主之者，帝曰：「朕亦聞之。」

translations.literal: Qi Fang, metropolitan commander of Zhenjiang, was punished for extortion; chief minister Chen Junqing said inner attendants were behind it; the Emperor said: "I too have heard."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fang, metropolitan commander of Zhenjiang, was punished for extortion. Chief minister Chen Junqing said inner attendants were behind it. The Emperor said, "I too have heard."

sentences.zh: 乃以內侍陳瑜、李宗回等付大理獄，究其賂狀，獄成，決配之。

translations.literal: He then handed inner attendants Chen Yu, Li Zonghui, and others to the Court of Judicial Review prison, investigated their bribery, and when the case was complete sentenced them to assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He handed inner attendants Chen Yu, Li Zonghui, and others to the Court of Judicial Review, investigated their bribery, and when the case was complete sentenced them to assignment.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年下詔曰：「獄，重事也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao an edict was issued: "Prisons are weighty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 2 an edict declared, "Prisons are weighty affairs.

sentences.zh: 用法一傾，則民無所措手足。

translations.literal: If application of law tilts once, the people have nowhere to place hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: If application of law tilts once, the people have nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，治獄之吏，巧持多端，隨意輕重之，朕甚患焉。

translations.literal: In recent years, officials who manage prisons have craftily held many devices and arbitrarily made severity or leniency—I am greatly troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, prison officials have craftily manipulated cases and arbitrarily adjusted severity—I am greatly troubled.

sentences.zh: 其自今革玩習之弊，明審克之公，使姦不容情，罰必當罪，用迪於刑之中，勉之哉，毋忽！」

translations.literal: From now reform the abuse of lax habit, clarify and scrutinize with impartiality, so that wrongdoing cannot hide in sentiment, punishments must match guilt, employ the mean in punishment—strive, do not neglect!"
translations.idiomatic: From now reform lax habits, judge with clarity and impartiality, let wrongdoing hide in no sentiment, let punishments match guilt, and employ the mean in punishment—strive and do not neglect!"

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「獄，重事也。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict: "Prisons are weighty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict declared, "Prisons are weighty affairs.

sentences.zh: 稽者有律，當者有比，疑者有讞。

translations.literal: Those who delay have the statutes; those who decide have precedents; those who doubt have deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Delay belongs to the law; judgment belongs to precedent; doubt belongs to deliberation.

sentences.zh: 比年顧以獄情白於執政，探取旨意，以為輕重 ，甚亡謂也。
