translations.literal: In recent years they have only reported prison circumstances to the chief ministers, probing and taking their intentions to determine severity or leniency—it is utterly absurd.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years officials have merely reported case details to the chief ministers, reading their intentions to set severity or leniency—a practice utterly devoid of principle.

sentences.zh: 自今其祗乃心，敬於刑，惟當為貴，毋習前非。

translations.literal: From now reverently devote your hearts, respect punishment; only what is appropriate is prized; do not follow former errors.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, devote yourselves wholeheartedly to the law, treat punishment with reverence, hold proper judgment above all else, and do not repeat past abuses.

sentences.zh: 不如吾詔，吾將大寘於罰，罔攸赦。」

translations.literal: If you do not obey my edict, I shall greatly impose punishments; none shall be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Disobey this edict, and I shall impose severe punishment from which none shall be spared."

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：「以絹計贓者，更增一貫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict: "For those calculating embezzlement in silk, increase the amount by one string further.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict declared, "For embezzlement calculated in silk, raise the threshold by one string.

sentences.zh: 以四千為一匹。」

translations.literal: Take four thousand as one bolt."
translations.idiomatic: One bolt of silk was set at four thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 議者又言：「犯盜，以敕計錢定罪，以律計絹。

translations.literal: Discussants also said: "For theft offenses, use the edict to calculate by cash for conviction, use the code to calculate by silk.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists also argued, "For theft, convictions under the edict are calculated in cash, while those under the code are calculated in silk.

sentences.zh: 今律以絹定罪者遞增一千，敕內以錢定罪，亦合例增一千。」

translations.literal: Now where the code convicts by silk, increase by one thousand progressively; within the edict where convicting by cash, likewise increase by one thousand per precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Since silk-based convictions under the code are now raised by one thousand at each step, cash-based convictions under the edict should likewise be raised by one thousand."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 臨安府左右司理、府院三獄，杖直獄子以無所給，至為無籍。

translations.literal: Lin'an Prefecture's Left and Right Judicial Review offices and the three prisons of the prefectural court—cudgel supervisors and prison guards, for lack of pay, even became unregistered vagabonds.
translations.idiomatic: At the Left and Right Judicial Review offices and the three prefectural prisons of Lin'an, cudgel supervisors and prison guards went unpaid and sank so low as to become unregistered drifters.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：「人月給錢十貫，米六斗，每院止許置一十二人。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict: "Each person monthly given ten strings of cash and six dou of rice; each prison may employ only twelve persons."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, an edict ordered ten strings of cash and six dou of rice per person per month, with no more than twelve staff allowed in each prison."

sentences.zh: 時州縣獄禁淹延，八年，詔：「徒以上罪入禁三月者，提刑司類申刑部，置籍立限以督之。」

translations.literal: At the time prefecture and county imprisonments dragged on; in the eighth year, an edict: "Those sentenced to forced labor or above and detained three months, the circuit judicial intendants report by category to the Ministry of Justice, establish registers and set deadlines to supervise."
translations.idiomatic: As detention in prefecture and county prisons dragged on, in the eighth year an edict required circuit judicial intendants to report to the Ministry of Justice, by category, all cases of forced-labor offenders or above held three months or more, and to keep registers with deadlines for enforcement."

sentences.zh: 其後，又詔中書置禁，奏取會籍，大臣按閱，以察刑寺稽違，與夫不應問難而問難，不應會而會者。

translations.literal: Subsequently, another edict ordered the Central Secretariat to establish detention records, memorialize and compare registers, and ministers to review them, to inspect delays and violations by the judicial offices, and those who pose questions in debate when questions should not be posed, or hold joint deliberations when they should not.
translations.idiomatic: Later, another edict required the Central Secretariat to keep detention records, submit them for comparison, and have senior ministers review them to detect delays at the judicial offices and improper questioning or joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 淳熙初，浙西提刑鄭興裔上檢驗格目，詔頒之諸路提刑司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunxi, Zhexi Judicial Intendant Zheng Xingyi submitted inspection criteria; an edict promulgated them to all circuit judicial intendant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunxi era, Zhexi Judicial Intendant Zheng Xingyi submitted standards for forensic inspection, and an edict ordered them promulgated to every circuit judicial intendant office.

sentences.zh: 凡檢覆必給三本：一申所屬，一申本司，一給被害之家。

translations.literal: For every re-inspection three copies must be issued: one submitted to the subordinate office, one to this office, one given to the victim's family.
translations.idiomatic: Every re-inspection had to produce three copies: one for the subordinate office, one for the intendant's office, and one for the victim's family.

sentences.zh: 紹興法，鞫獄官推勘不得實，故有不當者，一案坐之。

translations.literal: Under the Shaoxing code, if interrogating prison officials' investigation did not obtain the truth and therefore there was impropriety, they were punished in one case.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shaoxing law, if an interrogating official failed to establish the facts and judgment was improper, the entire case was held against him.

sentences.zh: 乾道法，又恐有移替事故者，即致淹延，乃令先決罪人不當，官吏案後收坐。

translations.literal: Under the Qiandao code, fearing transfer or replacement incidents would cause delay, it ordered first deciding the guilty party's impropriety, with officials punished afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qiandao law, fearing that transfers and replacements would cause delay, officials were told to decide the defendant's case first and hold the responsible officers accountable afterward.

sentences.zh: 至是，所司請更定死罪依紹興法，餘依乾道施行，從之。

translations.literal: At this time, the relevant office requested re-establishing that death sentences follow Shaoxing law and the remainder follow Qiandao implementation; approved.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the responsible office asked that capital cases again follow Shaoxing law while all others follow Qiandao practice; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 其後，有司以覆勘不同，則前官有失入之罪，往往雷同前勘。

translations.literal: Subsequently, because offices held that if re-investigation differed, then prior officials had the crime of excessive sentencing, they often merely echoed the prior investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, since a differing re-investigation would expose prior officials to charges of excessive sentencing, they often simply copied the earlier findings.

sentences.zh: 帝知其弊，十四年，詔特免一案推結一次。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew this abuse; in the fourteenth year, an edict specially exempted one case of investigation and conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor saw the abuse, and in the fourteenth year issued an edict granting a one-time exemption from the single-case liability rule for investigation and conclusion.

sentences.zh: 於是小大之獄，多得其情。

translations.literal: Thereupon in large and small prisons, the truth of cases was mostly obtained.
translations.idiomatic: After that, large and small cases alike more often reached the truth.

sentences.zh: 二廣州軍獄吏，畏憲司點檢送勘之害，凡有重囚，多斃於獄。

translations.literal: Prison clerks of the Two Guang circuits' prefectures and military districts, fearing the harm of judicial commissioners' inspection and referral for investigation—for every serious prisoner, many died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Guang circuits, prison clerks feared the harm of judicial commissioners' inspections and referrals for investigation, and many serious prisoners died in custody.

sentences.zh: 臣僚以為請，乃詔二廣提刑司詳覆公事，若小節不完，不須追逮獄吏，委本州究實保明；

translations.literal: Officials memorialized on this; an edict ordered the Two Guang judicial intendant circuits to re-investigate official business; if minor points were incomplete, prison clerks need not be pursued and arrested; delegate to the home prefecture to verify and certify;
translations.idiomatic: When officials memorialized on the matter, an edict ordered the Two Guang judicial intendant circuits to re-examine cases; if only minor details were incomplete, prison clerks were not to be pursued, and the home prefecture was to verify and certify the facts;

sentences.zh: 遇有死者，必根究其所以致死。

translations.literal: When there were deaths, the reason for death must be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prisoner died, the cause of death had to be thoroughly investigated.

sentences.zh: 三衙及江上諸軍，各有推獄，謂之「後司」。

translations.literal: The Three Palace Guard corps and the various armies on the river each had interrogation prisons, called the "rear offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Palace Guard corps and the armies stationed along the Yangzi each maintained their own interrogation prisons, known as the "rear offices."

sentences.zh: 獄成決于主帥，不經屬官，故軍吏多受財為奸。

translations.literal: When cases were complete they were decided by the commander-in-chief, not passing through subordinate officials; therefore military clerks often accepted bribes and committed wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Once a case was closed, judgment rested with the commander alone, bypassing subordinate officials, so military clerks often took bribes and abused their power.

sentences.zh: 光宗時，乃詔通曉條制屬官兼管之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Guangzong's time, an edict ordered subordinate officials versed in statutes to jointly supervise them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Guangzong, an edict required subordinate officials versed in statutes to share supervision of these offices.

sentences.zh: 廣東路瘴癘，惟英德府為最甚，謂之「人間生地獄」。

translations.literal: Guangdong Circuit has miasma; only Yingde Prefecture is most severe, called "hell on earth among the living."
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong was notorious for miasma, but Yingde Prefecture was worst of all—it was called "a living hell on earth."

sentences.zh: 諸司公事欲速成者，多送之，自非死罪，至即誣伏，亟就刑責以出。

translations.literal: Various offices wanting quick resolution of official business often sent cases there; unless the crime was capital, upon arrival prisoners immediately falsely confessed and hastily accepted punishment to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Offices seeking quick closure often sent cases there; unless the charge was capital, prisoners would falsely confess on arrival and accept punishment at once to escape.

sentences.zh: 五年，臣僚言之，詔：「本路諸司公事應送別州者，無送英德府。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, officials spoke of it; an edict: "Official business of all offices in this circuit that should be sent to other prefectures—do not send to Yingde Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after officials raised the issue, an edict declared, "Official cases in this circuit that should be transferred to another prefecture must not be sent to Yingde."

sentences.zh: 至寧宗時，刑獄滋濫。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ningzong's time, criminal prisons grew ever more excessive.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of Emperor Ningzong, criminal justice had become ever more abusive.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰初，天下上死案，一全年千八百一十一人，而斷死者纔一百八十一人，餘皆貸之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiatai, empire-wide capital cases submitted—one full year, 1,811 persons; yet those actually sentenced to death were only 181; the rest were all commuted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiatai, 1,811 capital cases were submitted empire-wide in a single year, yet only 181 ended in execution; all the rest were commuted.

sentences.zh: 乃詔諸憲臺，歲終檢舉州軍有獄空?禁人少者，申省取旨。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all judicial commissioners: at year's end report prefectures and military districts with empty prisons and few detainees, submit to the ministry for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered all circuit judicial commissioners, at year's end, to report prefectures and military districts whose prisons stood empty or held few detainees, and submit the cases to the ministry for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年詔：「以絹計贓定罪者，江北鐵錢依四川法，二當銅錢一。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiading, an edict: "For those convicting embezzlement calculated in silk, north-of-the-river iron cash follows Sichuan law—two iron cash equal one copper cash."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 4 an edict declared, "For embezzlement calculated in silk, iron cash north of the Yangzi would follow Sichuan practice, with two iron cash counted as one copper cash."

sentences.zh: 江西提刑徐似道言：「檢驗官指輕作重，以有為無，差訛交互，以故吏姦出入人罪。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Judicial Intendant Xu Sidao said: "Inspection officials treat light injuries as heavy, treat what exists as nonexistent, errors interchanged—wherefore clerks corruptly enter and release persons from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Judicial Intendant Xu Sidao said, "Forensic inspectors treat light wounds as grave, deny what is plainly there, and swap errors back and forth, enabling clerks to corruptly convict the innocent or free the guilty.

sentences.zh: 乞以湖南正背人形隨格目給下，令於傷損去處，依樣朱紅書畫，唱喝傷痕，眾無異詞，然後署押。」

translations.literal: Request that Hunan's front-and-back human form diagrams accompany the criteria grid when issued; order that at injury locations they draw in vermilion per the model, announce wounds aloud; with no dissent from the assembly, then sign and seal."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Hunan's front-and-back body diagrams be issued with the standards, that wounds be marked in vermilion on the diagram at each injured spot, that the wounds be called out aloud, and that signatures be affixed only after all present agreed."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，頒之天下。

translations.literal: Edict approved; promulgated empire-wide.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved and promulgated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔三衙及江上、四川諸軍，以武舉人主管後司公事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered the Three Palace Guard corps and the armies on the river and in Sichuan to have military examination graduates supervise rear-office business.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, an edict required the Three Palace Guard corps and the armies on the Yangzi and in Sichuan to put military examination graduates in charge of rear-office business.

sentences.zh: 理宗起自民間，具知刑獄之弊。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong rose from common people and fully knew the abuses of criminal prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong had risen from common life and knew firsthand the abuses of the prisons.

sentences.zh: 初即位，即詔天下恤刑 ，又親制《審刑銘》以警有位。

translations.literal: Upon first taking the throne, he immediately issued an edict empire-wide mercy in punishment, and also personally composed the "Inscription on Judging Punishment" to warn those in office.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took the throne, he issued an empire-wide edict on merciful punishment and personally composed the Inscription on Judging Punishment to warn those in power.

sentences.zh: 每歲大暑，必臨軒慮囚。

translations.literal: Every year at great heat, he always held court to review prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Every year at the height of summer, he held court to review prisoners.

sentences.zh: 自謀殺、故殺、鬥殺已殺人者，偽造符印、會子，放火，官員犯入己贓，將校軍人犯枉法外，自餘死罪，情輕者降從流，流降從徒，徒從杖，杖已下釋之。

translations.literal: Apart from premeditated murder, intentional murder, brawling murder already resulting in death, forging seals and tally notes, arson, officials guilty of embezzlement for personal gain, and commanders and soldiers guilty of bending the law—of the remaining capital crimes, where circumstances were light, death was reduced to exile, exile to forced labor, forced labor to beating, and below beating they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Except for premeditated murder, intentional murder, brawling that ended in death, forging seals and paper notes, arson, official embezzlement, and military officers who bent the law, all other capital sentences were commuted one step: death to exile, exile to forced labor, forced labor to beating, and lesser punishments to release.

sentences.zh: 大寒慮囚，及祈晴祈雪及災祥，亦如之。

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners in great cold, and prayers for clear weather, snow, and auspicious or inauspicious omens—likewise.
translations.idiomatic: He did the same in deep winter, and likewise when praying for clear skies, for snow, or in response to omens of disaster or blessing.

sentences.zh: 有一歲凡數疏決者。

translations.literal: Some years there were several rounds of lenient release altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Some years saw several rounds of clemency in a single year.

sentences.zh: 後以建康亦先朝駐蹕之地，罪人亦得視臨安減降之法。

translations.literal: Later, because Jiankang was also a former imperial residence, convicts there also received Lin'an's reduction and clemency law.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Jiankang had also been an imperial residence, its convicts were granted the same reductions as those at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 帝之用刑可謂極厚矣，而天下之獄不勝其酷。

translations.literal: The Emperor's use of punishment could be called extremely lenient, yet empire-wide prisons were unbearably cruel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mercy in punishment could scarcely have been greater, yet prisons throughout the empire were unbearably cruel.

sentences.zh: 每歲冬夏，詔提刑行郡決囚，提刑憚行，悉委倅貳，倅貳不行，復委幕屬。

translations.literal: Every year in winter and summer, an edict ordered judicial intendants to travel their circuits to decide prisoners; judicial intendants feared traveling and all delegated to vice-prefects; vice-prefects would not go and again delegated to staff.
translations.idiomatic: Each winter and summer, edicts ordered judicial intendants to travel their circuits and decide cases, but they feared the duty and passed it to vice-prefects; when vice-prefects refused, it fell to clerical staff.

sentences.zh: 所委之人，類皆肆行威福，以要餽遺。

translations.literal: Those delegated were mostly the type who arbitrarily wielded power, to demand gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Those to whom the work was delegated were mostly men who abused their authority to extort gifts.

sentences.zh: 監司、郡守，擅作威福，意所欲黥，則令入其當黥之由，意所欲殺，則令證其當死之罪，呼喝吏卒，嚴限日時，監勒招承，催促結款。

translations.literal: Supervisory commissioners and prefects arbitrarily wielded power: for whomever they wished tattooed, they ordered entering the grounds warranting tattoo; for whomever they wished killed, they ordered proving the crime warranting death; they shouted at clerks and guards, set strict deadlines, supervised forced confession, and urged closing the case.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory commissioners and prefects abused their power at will: if they wanted a man tattooed, they ordered the grounds for tattooing entered; if they wanted him dead, they ordered proof of a capital offense fabricated; they shouted at clerks and guards, set strict deadlines, supervised forced confessions, and pressed for closed cases.

sentences.zh: 而又擅置獄具，非法殘民，或斷薪為杖，掊擊手足，名曰「掉柴」；

translations.literal: And moreover they arbitrarily installed prison implements and illegally mutilated people—or broke firewood into cudgels and beat hands and feet, called "dropping firewood";
translations.idiomatic: They also set up illegal torture devices: some broke firewood into clubs and beat prisoners' hands and feet, a method called "dropping firewood";

sentences.zh: 或木索?施，夾兩脰，名曰「夾幫」；

translations.literal: Or wood and rope were applied together, clamping both sides of the neck—this was called "Clamping the Jaw";
translations.idiomatic: Some used wood and rope together to squeeze both sides of the neck; they called it "jaw-clamping."

sentences.zh: 或纏繩於首，加以木楔，名曰「腦箍」；

translations.literal: Or rope was wound around the head and wooden wedges inserted—this was called the "Brain Ring";
translations.idiomatic: Some wound rope around the head and drove in wooden wedges; they called it the "brain ring."

sentences.zh: 或反縛跪地，短豎堅木，交辮兩股，令獄卒跳躍於上，謂之「超棍」，痛深骨髓，幾於殞命。

translations.literal: Or one was bound face-down kneeling, a short stout pole planted upright, the two legs braided together, and jailers made to leap upon it—this was called "Leaping the Pole"; the pain reached to the marrow, almost costing one's life.
translations.idiomatic: Some bound victims face down on their knees, planted a short hardwood post, braided their legs together, and had jailers jump on top—called "leap-the-pole." The agony pierced to the bone marrow and nearly cost victims their lives.

sentences.zh: 富貴之家，稍有 ，動籍其貲。

translations.literal: In wealthy and noble households, if there were the slightest entanglement or bias, their property was routinely confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: For affluent families, the slightest pretext was enough to trigger confiscation of their assets.

sentences.zh: 又以趁辦月樁及添助版帳為名，不問罪之輕重，並從科罰。

translations.literal: Also, under the names of meeting monthly quota contributions and supplementary registry payments, regardless of the severity of the offense, all were subject to penalties.
translations.idiomatic: They also levied fines in the name of meeting monthly supply quotas and supplemental ledger contributions, punishing offenders without regard to the gravity of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 大率官取其十，吏漁其百。

translations.literal: Generally, officials took a tenth, while clerks plundered a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, officials skimmed one part in ten, while underlings extorted ten times that much.

sentences.zh: 諸重刑，皆申提刑司詳覆，或具案奏裁，即無州縣專殺之理，往往殺之而待罪。

translations.literal: All heavy punishments were to be reported to the Office of Judicial Review for detailed reassessment, or the full case submitted for imperial decision—there was no principle by which prefectures and counties might execute on their own authority; yet they often executed first and then awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Serious sentences were supposed to be referred to the regional judicial inspectorate for review, or forwarded to the throne for a ruling—county and prefectural officials had no legal authority to put people to death on their own. Yet they often executed prisoners first and accepted punishment afterward.

sentences.zh: 法無拘鎖之條，特州縣一時彈壓盜賊姦暴，罪不至配者，故拘鎖之，俾之省愆，或一月、兩月，或一季、半年，雖永鎖者亦有期限，有口食。

translations.literal: The law had no provision for detention in shackles; it was only that prefectures and counties, to suppress bandits and violent crime for a time, detained those whose offenses did not warrant exile, so they might reflect on their faults—for one or two months, or a season, or half a year; even those detained indefinitely had time limits and rations.
translations.idiomatic: Statute law contained no general provision for shackled detention; counties and prefectures used it only as a temporary measure against banditry and violent crime, holding offenders whose crimes fell short of exile so they might mend their ways—for a month or two, a season, or half a year. Even indefinite detention was supposed to have limits and provide food.

sentences.zh: 是時，州縣殘忍，拘鎖者竟無限日，不支口食，淹滯囚係，死而後已。

translations.literal: At this time prefectures and counties were cruel; those detained had no limit on days, were given no rations, languished in confinement, and only ended when dead.
translations.idiomatic: By then local governments had grown savage: the detained were held without time limit, denied food, left to rot in jail until death released them.

sentences.zh: 又以己私摧折手足，拘鎖尉砦。

translations.literal: For private grudges they also broke hands and feet, and detained people in constabulary stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Driven by private malice, they maimed limbs and kept people shackled in constabulary forts.

sentences.zh: 亦有豪強賂吏，羅織平民而囚殺之。

translations.literal: There were also powerful bullies who bribed clerks to frame commoners and imprison and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Local strongmen also bribed officials to fabricate charges against commoners, then jailed and murdered them.

sentences.zh: 甚至戶婚詞訟，亦皆收禁。

translations.literal: Even lawsuits over household affairs and marriage were all taken into custody.
translations.idiomatic: Even civil disputes over marriages and household matters ended in detention.

sentences.zh: 有飲食不充，飢餓而死者；

translations.literal: Some died of hunger when food was insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Some starved to death for lack of adequate food;

sentences.zh: 有無力請求，吏卒凌虐而死者；

translations.literal: Some died under clerks' and jailers' abuse when they had no means to plead;
translations.idiomatic: Some, unable to buy relief, were tormented to death by clerks and guards;

sentences.zh: 有為兩詞賂遺，苦楚而死者。

translations.literal: Some died in torment because both parties in a suit gave bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Some perished under torture when both sides in a lawsuit paid bribes and officials made them suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 懼其發覺，先以病申，名曰「監醫」，實則已死；

translations.literal: Fearing discovery, they first reported illness—called "Medical Supervision"—when in fact the prisoner was already dead;
translations.idiomatic: Fearful of exposure, officials filed illness reports first—calling it "supervised medical care"—when the prisoner was already dead;

sentences.zh: 名曰「病死」，實則殺之。

translations.literal: Called "Death from Illness," when in fact they had been killed.
translations.idiomatic: They labeled it "death from natural illness" when they had in fact murdered the victim.

sentences.zh: 至度宗時，雖累詔切責而禁止之，終莫能勝，而國亡矣。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Duzong, though repeated edicts sternly condemned and forbade this, it could never be overcome, and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: By Duzong's reign, despite repeated stern edicts forbidding such abuses, nothing could stem them—and the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 詔獄，本以糾大姦慝，故其事不常見。

translations.literal: Imperial prisons by edict were originally meant to expose great treachery and wickedness; therefore such cases were not commonly seen.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial prisons established by edict were originally reserved for rooting out grave treachery; for that reason they were rarely invoked.

sentences.zh: 初，羣臣犯法，體大者多下御史臺獄，小則開封府、大理寺鞫治焉。

translations.literal: At first, when ministers violated the law, those of greater standing were mostly sent to the Censorate prison; lesser cases were tried by the Kaifeng Prefecture and the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when officials broke the law, senior figures were usually remanded to the Censorate prison, while lesser cases went to the Kaifeng Prefecture or the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 神宗以來，凡一時承詔置推者，謂之「制勘院」，事出中書，則曰「推勘院」，獄已迺罷。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Shenzong, whenever investigators were temporarily appointed by edict, the office was called the "Commissioned Investigation Court"; when the matter came from the Secretariat, it was called the "Examination and Investigation Court"—and once the case was closed, the office was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: From Shenzong's reign onward, ad hoc tribunals appointed to investigate under imperial order were called "commissioned investigation courts"; when the Secretariat took charge, they were called "examination courts." They were disbanded once the case concluded.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，命尚書都官郎中沈衡鞫前知杭州祖無擇于秀州，內侍乘驛追逮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, Director of the Bureau of Revenue in the Ministry of Justice Shen Heng was ordered to try Zu Wuzhe, former prefect of Hangzhou, at Xiuzhou; an inner palace attendant rode post-horses in pursuit to bring him in.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xining era (1069), Shen Heng, director in the Ministry of Justice's revenue bureau, was assigned to try Zu Wuzhe, former prefect of Hangzhou, at Xiuzhou. An imperial attendant was dispatched by relay horse to seize him.

sentences.zh: 御史張戩等言：「無擇三朝近侍，而驟繫囹圄，非朝廷以廉恥風厲臣下之意，請免其就獄，止就審問。」

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Jian and others said: "Wuzhe was a close attendant through three reigns, yet he was suddenly bound in prison—this is not the court's intent to foster integrity and shame among officials; we ask that he be spared entering prison and only be examined."
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhang Jian and others protested: "Wuzhe served as a close attendant through three reigns, yet he was suddenly thrown into prison. That is hardly how the court teaches officials to value honor and shame. We ask that he be spared confinement and questioned only."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not comply.

sentences.zh: 又命崇文院校書張載鞫前知明州、光祿卿苗振于越州。

translations.literal: Also ordered Academician-Scribe Zhang Zai of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature to try Miao Zhen, former prefect of Mingzhou and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, at Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zai, a proofreader of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature, was also assigned to try Miao Zhen, former prefect of Mingzhou and Minister of the Imperial Household, at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 獄成，無擇坐貸官錢及借公使酒，謫忠正軍節度副使，振坐故入裴士堯罪及所為不法，謫復州團練副使。

translations.literal: When the cases were concluded, Wuzhe was found guilty of embezzling official funds and borrowing public envoy wine, and was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army; Zhen was found guilty of intentionally framing Pei Shiyao and other unlawful acts, and was demoted to Vice Training Commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The trials concluded: Wuzhe was convicted of misappropriating official funds and borrowing government hospitality wine, and was demoted to vice commissioner of the Zhongzheng Army; Zhen was convicted of maliciously framing Pei Shiyao and other misconduct, and was demoted to vice training commissioner at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 獄半年乃決，辭所連逮官吏，坐勒停、衝替、編管又十餘人，皆御史王子韶啟其事。

translations.literal: The prison cases took half a year to decide; those implicated in testimony included more than ten officials punished by suspension, replacement, and supervised exile—all initiated by Censor Wang Zishao.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year passed before the cases were resolved. More than ten implicated officials received punishments ranging from suspension and replacement to supervised exile—all of it set in motion by Censor Wang Zishao.

sentences.zh: 自是詔獄屢興，其悖于法及國體所繫者著之，其餘不足紀也。

translations.literal: From this time imperial prisons by edict arose repeatedly; those cases that violated law and touched the body politic are recorded here; the rest are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, imperial prisons proliferated. Those cases that violated statute and implicated the nation's integrity are recorded here; the rest need not be set down.

sentences.zh: 八年，沂州民朱唐告前餘姚主簿李逢謀反。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Zhu Tang, a commoner of Yizhou, reported that Li Feng, former registrar of Yuyao, had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (of Xining), Zhu Tang, a commoner from Yizhou, accused Li Feng, former registrar of Yuyao, of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 提點刑獄王庭筠言其無迹，但謗讟，語涉指斥及妄說休咎，請編配。

translations.literal: Judicial Inspector Wang Tingyun said there was no evidence, only slander; the words involved personal attacks and reckless talk of fortune and misfortune; he requested exile registration.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial inspector Wang Tingyun held that there was no evidence of treason—only slander involving personal attacks and reckless fortune-telling—and recommended banishment.

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，遣御史臺推直官蹇周輔劾治。

translations.literal: The Emperor was doubtful and dispatched Jian Zhoufu, direct investigator of the Censorate, to impeach and prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remained skeptical and sent Jian Zhoufu, a direct investigator of the Censorate, to take up the case.

sentences.zh: 中書以庭筠所奏不當， ?劾之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat held Tingyun's report improper and also impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat deemed Wang Tingyun's report inadequate and impeached him as well.

sentences.zh: 庭筠懼，自縊死。

translations.literal: Tingyun, in fear, hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingyun, terrified, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 逢辭連宗室秀州團練使世居、醫官劉育等、河中府觀察推官徐革，詔捕繫臺獄，命中丞鄧綰、同知諫院范百祿與御史徐禧雜治。

translations.literal: Feng's testimony implicated Shijiu, Training Commissioner of Xiuzhou of the imperial clan, Medical Officer Liu Yu, and Xu Ge, investigating officer of the Hezhong Circuit observation commission; an edict ordered their arrest and imprisonment in the Censorate prison, and Vice Commissioner Deng Wan, Vice Director of Remonstrance Fan Bailu, and Censor Xu Xi were appointed to try the case jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation, Li Feng implicated Shijiu, a training commissioner of Xiuzhou and member of the imperial clan, the medical officer Liu Yu, and Xu Ge, a judicial investigator in the Hezhong Circuit. An edict ordered their arrest and confinement in the Censorate prison, with Vice Commissioner Deng Wan, Vice Director of Remonstrance Fan Bailu, and Censor Xu Xi assigned to hear the case jointly.

sentences.zh: 獄具，賜世居死，李逢、劉育及徐革並凌遲處死，將作監主簿張靖、武進士郝士宣皆腰斬，司天監學生秦彪、百姓李士寧杖脊，並湖南編管。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, Shijiu was granted death; Li Feng, Liu Yu, and Xu Ge were all executed by dismemberment; Assistant Director Zhang Jing of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and military graduate Hao Shixuan were both cut in two at the waist; Astronomy Bureau student Qin Biao and commoner Li Shineng were flogged on the back and all were registered for exile in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The case concluded: Shijiu was granted death; Li Feng, Liu Yu, and Xu Ge were put to death by lingchi (slow slicing); Zhang Jing, assistant director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and Hao Shixuan, a military examination graduate, were cut in two at the waist; Qin Biao, a student of the Astronomy Bureau, and the commoner Li Shineng were flogged and banished to Hunan under supervised exile.

sentences.zh: 餘連逮者追官落職。

translations.literal: The remaining implicated persons had their posts revoked and ranks stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Others implicated in the case were stripped of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 世居子孫貸死除名，削屬籍。

translations.literal: Shijiu's descendants were spared execution but removed from the register and struck from the clan rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiu's descendants were spared execution but removed from official registers and expunged from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 舊勘鞫官吏並劾罪。

translations.literal: The former examining officials were all impeached and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who had earlier handled the investigation were impeached and punished as well.

sentences.zh: 李士寧者，挾術出入貴人門，常見世居母康，以仁宗御製詩上之。

translations.literal: Li Shineng, relying on arts, moved in and out among the gates of the noble; he often saw Shijiu's mother Kang and presented to her poems composed by Emperor Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shineng practiced occult arts and moved among the great houses. He often visited Shijiu's mother, Lady Kang, bearing poems composed by Emperor Renzong.

sentences.zh: 百祿謂士寧熒惑世居致不軌，且疑知其逆謀，推問不服。

translations.literal: Bailu said Shineng had beguiled Shijiu into wrongdoing and suspected he knew of the plot; under interrogation he did not confess.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bailu maintained that Li Shineng had led Shijiu astray toward treason and suspected he knew of the plot. Under interrogation, Li Shineng would not confess.

sentences.zh: 禧乃奏：「士寧贈詩，實仁宗御製，今獄官以為反因，臣不敢同。」

translations.literal: Xi then memorialized: "The poems Shineng presented were truly composed by Emperor Renzong; now the prison officials treat them as evidence of rebellion—I dare not agree."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi memorialized: "The poems Li Shineng gave were genuinely composed by Emperor Renzong. To treat them now as evidence of rebellion—I cannot assent to that."

sentences.zh: 百祿以士寧嘗與王安石善，欲鍛鍊附致妖言死罪，卒論士寧徒罪，而奏「禧故出之，以媚大臣」。

translations.literal: Bailu, because Shineng had once been friendly with Wang Anshi, wished to forge a case and attach charges of seditious speech to bring a capital sentence; in the end Shineng was sentenced only to exile, and Bailu memorialized that "Xi deliberately exonerated him to flatter great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bailu, noting Li Shineng's former friendship with Wang Anshi, tried to fabricate charges and attach seditious-speech counts to secure a capital sentence. Li Shineng was ultimately sentenced only to exile. Fan Bailu then accused Xu Xi of deliberately exonerating him "to curry favor with powerful ministers."

sentences.zh: 詔詳劾理曲者以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a thorough investigation of those who had distorted the facts to be reported.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a full investigation: those who had perverted justice were to be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 百祿坐報上不實，落職。

translations.literal: Bailu was punished for reporting falsely to the throne and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Bailu was found guilty of submitting false reports to the throne and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 若凌遲、腰斬之法，熙寧以前未嘗用於元凶巨，而自是以口語狂悖致罪者，麗于極法矣。

translations.literal: As for the punishments of dismemberment and waist-cutting, before Xining they had never been applied to arch-criminals and great pests; from this time those who incurred guilt through reckless and disrespectful speech were subject to the extreme law.
translations.idiomatic: The penalties of lingchi and waist-cutting had never before Xining been applied even to arch-criminals and notorious malefactors; from this case onward, men condemned for rash and disrespectful words could face the harshest punishments on the books.

sentences.zh: 蓋詔獄之興，始由柄國之臣藉此以威縉紳，逞其私憾，朋黨之禍遂起，流毒不已。

translations.literal: Generally, the rise of imperial prisons began when ministers holding state power used them to intimidate the gentry and satisfy private resentments; the disaster of factional strife then arose, and its poison flowed on without end.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prison arose when men who held the reins of state used it to intimidate the official class and settle private scores. Factional strife followed, and its poison spread without end.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間，章惇、蔡卞用事，既再追貶呂公著、司馬光，及謫呂大防等嶺外，意猶未快，仍用黃履疏高士京狀追貶王珪，皆誣以「圖危上躬」，其言寖及宣仁，上頗惑之。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, Zhang Dun and Cai Bian held power; having twice posthumously demoted Lü Gongzhu and Sima Guang, and exiled Lü Dafang and others beyond the Ling Mountains, they were still not satisfied, and used Huang Lü's memorial and Gao Shijing's report to posthumously demote Wang Gui—all slandered as "plotting to endanger the Emperor's person"; their words gradually implicated Empress Xuanren, and the Emperor was much swayed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng reign period, Zhang Dun and Cai Bian dominated the court. Having already posthumously demoted Lü Gongzhu and Sima Guang and banished Lü Dafang and others beyond the mountains, they were still not satisfied. Invoking memorials by Huang Lü and Gao Shijing, they posthumously demoted Wang Gui as well—all on the fabricated charge of "plotting against the Emperor's person." Their accusations gradually reached Empress Xuanren, and the emperor was deeply unsettled.

sentences.zh: 最後，起同文館獄，將悉誅元祐舊臣。

translations.literal: Finally they raised the Tongwen Hall case, intending to execute all the old ministers of the Yuanyou era.
translations.idiomatic: At last they opened the Tongwen Hall case, intending to put to death the entire Yuanyou-era old guard.

sentences.zh: 時太府寺主簿蔡渭奏：「臣叔父碩，嘗於邢恕處見文及甫元祐中所寄恕書，具述姦臣大逆不道之謀。

translations.literal: At that time Assistant Director Cai Wei of the Imperial Granary memorialized: "My uncle Shuo once saw at Xing Shu's place a letter sent by Wen Jifu to Shu during the Yuanyou era, fully describing the treacherous ministers' designs of great rebellion and iniquity.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director Cai Wei of the Imperial Granary memorialized: "My uncle Shuo once saw at Xing Shu's home a letter Wen Jifu had sent to Shu during the Yuanyou period, laying out in detail a treasonous conspiracy by disloyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 及甫，彥博子也，必知姦狀。」

translations.literal: Jifu was Yanbo's son; he must have known the treacherous circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was the son of Yanbo; he must have known the full extent of the plot.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林承旨蔡京、吏部侍郎安惇同究問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hanlin Chancellor Cai Jing and Vice Minister of Personnel An Dun to investigate and question the matter jointly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Hanlin Chancellor Cai Jing and Vice Minister of Personnel An Dun to conduct a joint inquiry.

sentences.zh: 初，及甫與恕書，自謂：「畢禫當求外，入朝之計未可必，聞已逆為機，以榛塞其塗。」

translations.literal: At first, in Jifu's letter to Shu, he wrote of himself: "When the mourning rites are finished I should seek an outer post; the plan to enter court cannot yet be settled; I hear they have already seized on this as an opportunity, using brambles to block my path.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in a letter Jifu sent to Shu, he had written: "When mourning ends I ought to seek a provincial posting; my plan to return to court is still uncertain. I hear they have already turned this to their advantage, heaping obstacles in my way.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「司馬昭之心，路人所知。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Sima Zhao's heart is known even to passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "What Sima Zhao intends is plain to every passerby on the road.

sentences.zh: 又云：「濟之以粉昆，朋類錯立，欲以眇躬為甘心快意之地。」

translations.literal: He also said: "With Fen-kun added to assist, factions of partisans stand arrayed; they wish to make this slight person a place of satisfaction and contentment.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "With their allies in place and their clique arrayed around them, they mean to make a victim of me for their own satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 及甫嘗語蔡碩，謂司馬昭指劉摯，粉昆指韓忠彥，眇躬，及甫自謂。

translations.literal: Jifu once told Cai Shuo, saying Sima Zhao referred to Liu Zhi, Fen-kun referred to Han Zhongyan, and miao-gong—Jifu meant himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had once told Cai Shuo that "Sima Zhao" meant Liu Zhi, "Fen-kun" meant Han Zhongyan, and "this slight person" meant himself.

sentences.zh: 蓋俗稱駙馬都尉為「粉侯」，人以王師約故，呼其父克臣 為「粉父」，忠彥乃嘉彥之兄也。

translations.literal: For the common people called the imperial son-in-law "Fen Marquis"; because of Wang Shiyue, people called his father Kechen "Fen Father"; Zhongyan was Jiayan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The popular name for an imperial son-in-law was "Fen Marquis"; because Wang Shiyue was one, people called his father Kechen "Fen Father." Zhongyan was the elder brother of Jiayan.

sentences.zh: 及甫除都司，為劉摯論列。

translations.literal: When Jifu was appointed to the Capital Office, Liu Zhi denounced him in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Jifu was appointed to the Capital Office, Liu Zhi memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 又摯嘗論彥博不可除三省長官，故止為平章重事。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhi had once argued that Yanbo should not be removed as head of the Three Departments, so he was only made Grand Mentor Concurrent with the Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had also argued that Yanbo ought not be removed as chief of the Three Departments; as a result Yanbo was given only the title Grand Mentor Concurrent with State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及彥博致仕，及甫自權侍郎以修撰守郡，母喪除，與恕書請補外，因為躁忿詆毀之辭。

translations.literal: When Yanbo retired, Jifu went from acting vice minister to compiler serving as prefect; when his mother's mourning ended, he wrote to Shu requesting an outer appointment, and vented angry, slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanbo retired, Jifu served as acting vice minister and then as compiler turned prefect. When his mourning period ended, he wrote to Shu asking for a provincial post and filled the letter with angry abuse.

sentences.zh: 及置對，則以昭比摯如舊，眇躬乃以指上，而粉昆乃謂指王巖叟面如傅粉，故曰「粉」，梁燾字况之，以「况」為兄，故曰「昆」，斥摯將謀廢立，不利於上躬。

translations.literal: When questioned face to face, he claimed Zhao referred to Zhi as before, miao-gong meant the Emperor, and Fen-kun meant Wang Yansou, whose face was like powdered flour, hence "fen"; Liang Can styled Zhizhi, taking "kuang" as elder brother, hence "kun"—denouncing Zhi for plotting deposition, to the Emperor's harm.
translations.idiomatic: Under interrogation, he insisted that "Zhao" still meant Zhi, that "this slight person" referred to the Emperor, and that "Fen-kun" meant Wang Yansou—"fen" because his face looked powdered, "kun" because Liang Can's courtesy name Zhizhi treated "kuang" as elder brother—accusing Zhi of plotting a deposition harmful to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 京、惇言：「事涉不順，及甫止聞其父言，無他證佐，望別差官審問。」

translations.literal: Jing and Dun said: "The matter involves disloyal speech; Jifu heard only his father's words, with no other corroboration; we hope another official may be specially assigned to conduct inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Dun argued: "The case turns on treasonous language, but Jifu had heard only what his father said, with no other corroboration. We ask that another official be assigned to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 乃詔中書舍人蹇序辰審問，仍差內侍一員同往。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Secretariat Drafter Jian Xuchen to conduct inquiry, and also dispatched one inner attendant to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then assigned Secretariat Drafter Jian Xuchen to conduct the inquiry, with one palace eunuch sent along.

sentences.zh: 蔡京、安惇等共治之，將大有所誅戮，然卒不得其要領。

translations.literal: Cai Jing, An Dun, and others jointly handled the case, intending great executions, yet in the end never grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, An Dun, and their allies pursued the case together, intending mass executions, but never managed to pin down the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 會星變，上怒稍息，然京、惇極力鍛鍊不少置。

translations.literal: When a stellar omen occurred, the Emperor's wrath eased somewhat, yet Jing and Dun exerted themselves to forge the case and would not let up.
translations.idiomatic: A celestial anomaly intervened and the emperor's anger eased somewhat, but Jing and Dun redoubled their efforts to fabricate the case and would not relent.

sentences.zh: 既而梁燾卒於化州，劉摯卒於新州，眾皆疑二人不得其死。

translations.literal: Soon Liang Can died at Huazhou and Liu Zhi at Xinzhou; all suspected the two had not met natural deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Can soon died in exile at Huazhou and Liu Zhi at Xinzhou; many suspected they had not died naturally.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，詔：「摯、燾據文及甫等所供言語，偶逐人皆亡，不及考驗，明正典刑 。

translations.literal: The next year, in the fifth month, an edict said: "Zhi and Can, based on the statements supplied by Wen Jifu and others—the persons pursued happened all to be dead and could not be examined; let the proper punishments be clearly applied.
translations.idiomatic: The following May an edict declared: "On the testimony of Wen Jifu and others against Zhi and Can, the accused are already dead and cannot be cross-examined; the prescribed penalties shall be formally applied.

sentences.zh: 摯、燾諸子並勒停，永不收敘。」

translations.literal: The sons of Zhi and Can were all suspended from office and never again enrolled for service.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Zhi and Can were stripped of office and permanently barred from official appointment.

sentences.zh: 先時，三省進呈，帝曰：「摯等已謫遐方，朕遵祖宗遺志，未嘗殺戮大臣，其釋勿治。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Three Departments submitted the memorial, the Emperor said: "Zhi and the others have already been banished to distant regions; I follow the testament of the ancestors and have never executed great ministers; release them and do not punish."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Three Departments submitted the proposal, the emperor said: "Zhi and the others have already been exiled to distant posts. Following our ancestors' example, I have never put senior ministers to death. Drop the matter."

sentences.zh: 初，元祐更政，嘗置訴理所，申理濫。

translations.literal: At first, during the Yuanyou change of government, an Appeal Review Office was once established to redress abuses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou restoration, an Appeal Review Office had been set up to rectify wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，中丞安惇言：「神宗厲精圖治，明審庶獄，而陛下未親政時，姦臣置訴理所，凡得罪熙寧、元豐之間者，咸為除雪，歸怨先朝，收恩私室。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Censor-in-Chief An Dun said: "Shenzong vigorously applied himself to ordering the realm and clearly examined all cases, yet while Your Majesty had not yet taken personal rule, treacherous ministers established an Appeal Review Office; all who had been punished during the Xining and Yuanfeng periods were cleared of guilt, shifting blame to the former reign and gathering favor in private households.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1, Censor-in-Chief An Dun memorialized: "Shenzong worked tirelessly to govern and reviewed cases with care. Yet while Your Majesty had not yet assumed personal rule, disloyal ministers set up an Appeal Review Office and cleared every conviction from the Xining and Yuanfeng eras—shifting blame onto the previous reign while collecting gratitude for themselves.

sentences.zh: 乞取公案，看詳從初加罪之意，復依元斷施行。」

translations.literal: I ask that the case files be taken and examined in detail for the original intent of the convictions, and that the original sentences be re-imposed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the case files be reviewed to recover the original grounds for conviction, and that the original sentences be reinstated.

sentences.zh: 時章惇猶豫未應，蔡卞即以「相公二心」之言迫之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Dun hesitated and did not respond; Cai Bian then pressed him with words of "My lord has two hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun hesitated, and Cai Bian pressed him by accusing him of divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 惇懼，即日置局，命蹇序辰同安惇看詳案內文狀陳述，及訴理所看詳於先朝言語不順者，具名以聞。

translations.literal: Dun feared this and that same day established a bureau, ordering Jian Xuchen together with An Dun to examine in detail the statements in the case files, and those whom the Appeal Review Office had cleared for disloyal speech toward the former reign—to report their names.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Dun set up a review bureau that same day. He ordered Jian Xuchen and An Dun to scrutinize the case files and identify everyone the Appeal Review Office had cleared on charges of disloyal speech toward the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 自是，以伸雪復改正重得罪者八百三十家。

translations.literal: From this time, eight hundred thirty families who had been cleared and then re-sentenced were again found guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, eight hundred thirty families who had been exonerated through the appeal process were convicted again.

sentences.zh: 及徽宗即位，改正元祐訴理之人。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, those cleared through Yuanyou appeals were again corrected.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, the Yuanyou-era appeal reversals were themselves reversed.

sentences.zh: 右正言陳瓘言：「訴理得罪，自語言不順之外，改正者七百餘人。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Chen Guan said: "Of those punished through the appeal review, apart from disloyal speech, more than seven hundred had their sentences corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Chen Guan memorialized: "Aside from charges of disloyal speech, more than seven hundred people had their Yuanyou appeal victories overturned.

sentences.zh: 無罪者既蒙昭雪，則看詳之官如蹇序辰、安惇者，安可以不加罪乎？

translations.literal: If the innocent have already been cleared, how can examining officials such as Jian Xuchen and An Dun not be punished?
translations.idiomatic: If the innocent have been vindicated, how can officials such as Jian Xuchen and An Dun, who engineered the reversals, escape punishment?

sentences.zh: 序辰與惇受大臣諷諭，迎合紹述之意，因謂訴理之事，形迹先朝，遂使紛紛不已。

translations.literal: Xuchen and Dun, having received hints from great ministers, accommodated the intent to "continue the legacy," and treating the appeal-review cases as bearing on the former reign, caused endless turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Prompted by senior ministers, Xuchen and Dun shaped their findings to fit the "restore the legacy" agenda. Treating every appeal as an affront to the previous reign, they kept the controversy alive.

sentences.zh: 考之公議，宜正典刑。」

translations.literal: Measured against public opinion, the proper punishments should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion demanded that they receive the penalties the law prescribed.

sentences.zh: 會中書省亦請治惇、序辰罪，詔蹇序辰、安惇並除名，放歸田里。

translations.literal: The Secretariat also requested that Dun and Xuchen be punished; an edict stripped Jian Xuchen and An Dun of rank and sent them back to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat joined in calling for Dun and Xuchen to be punished. An edict stripped Jian Xuchen and An Dun of their ranks and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 靖康初元，既戮梁方平，太傅王黼責授崇信軍節度副使，永州安置。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, after Liang Fangping was executed, Grand Preceptor Wang Fu was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Chongxin and assigned to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, after Liang Fangping was put to death, Grand Preceptor Wang Fu was demoted to vice commissioner of the Chongxin Army and exiled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論黼欺君罔上，專權怙寵，財害民，壞法敗國，朔方之釁，黼主其謀。

translations.literal: Memorialists argued that Fu deceived the ruler and betrayed superiors, monopolized power and relied on favor, harmed the people through wealth, ruined law and defeated the state, and that Fu had masterminded the northern frontier disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that Fu had deceived the throne, abused his power, enriched himself at the people's expense, subverted the law, and ruined the state—and that he had been the architect of the northern frontier catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 遣吏追至雍丘殺之，取其首以獻，仍籍其家。

translations.literal: Officers were sent in pursuit; he was killed at Yongqiu, his head taken and presented, and his property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Agents were dispatched in pursuit; he was killed at Yongqiu, his head presented as proof, and his estate seized.

sentences.zh: 又詔賜拱衞大夫、安德軍承宣使李彥死。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered the death of Li Yan, Defender-in-Chief of the Guard and Commissioner of Ande.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered the execution of Li Yan, Defender-in-Chief of the Guard and commissioner of the Ande Army.

sentences.zh: 彥根括民田，奪民常產，重斂租課，百姓失業，愁怨溢路，官吏稍忤意，捃摭送獄，多至憤死，故特誅之。

translations.literal: Yan had seized commoners' fields through consolidation, seized their regular property, heavily levied rents and taxes; the people lost their livelihoods and resentment filled the roads; officials who slightly displeased him were gathered up and sent to prison, many dying of rage—therefore he was specially executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had confiscated private farmland, stripped people of their holdings, and imposed crushing taxes. Unemployment and outrage filled the roads. Officials who crossed him were hauled into prison on trumped-up charges—many dying there in fury. For this he was singled out for execution.

sentences.zh: 暴少保梁師成朋比王黼之罪，責彰化軍節度副使，行一日，追殺之。

translations.literal: The crimes of Junior Guardian Liang Shicheng in collusion with Wang Fu were exposed; he was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Zhanghua; after one day's travel he was pursued and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Guardian Liang Shicheng's collusion with Wang Fu was exposed. Demoted to vice commissioner of the Zhanghua Army, he was pursued and killed after only one day on the road.

sentences.zh: 臺諫極論朱肆行姦惡，起花石綱，竭百姓膏血，罄州縣帑藏，子姪承宣、觀察者數人，廝役為橫行，媵妾有封號，園第器用悉擬宮禁。

translations.literal: Censorial remonstrators passionately denounced Zhu Shi's villainy: launching the Flower and Stone Convoys, draining the people's blood, emptying prefectural treasuries; several nephews and sons held commissioner and observer posts; servants roamed lawlessly; concubines held noble titles; gardens, mansions, and utensils all matched the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censors denounced Zhu Shi for launching the Flower and Stone Convoys, bleeding the people dry and draining prefectural coffers. Several nephews held high military commissions; servants ran rampant; concubines bore noble titles; his gardens and furnishings rivaled the imperial palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，竄廣南，尋賜死。

translations.literal: In the third month he was banished to Guangnan; soon he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was exiled to Guangnan; soon afterward he was executed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 趙良嗣者，本燕人馬植。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangsi was originally Ma Zhi of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Liangsi had originally been Ma Zhi, a man of Yan.

sentences.zh: 政和初，童貫使遼國，植邀於路，說以覆宗國之策，貫挾之以歸，卒用其計，以基南北之禍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenghe era, Tong Guan went on mission to Liao; Zhi intercepted him on the road and urged a strategy to overthrow his own state; Guan brought him back and ultimately used his plan, laying the foundation for the calamity between north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenghe reign, when Tong Guan was sent to Liao, Ma Zhi waylaid him with a plan to destroy his own country. Tong Guan brought him back and eventually adopted his scheme, setting the stage for the catastrophe that divided north and south.

sentences.zh: 至是，伏誅。

translations.literal: At this time he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 七月，暴童貫十罪，遣人即所至斬之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Tong Guan's ten crimes were exposed; men were sent to behead him wherever he was found.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Tong Guan's ten crimes were publicly enumerated; agents were dispatched to behead him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 九月，言者論蔡攸興燕山之役，禍及天下，驕奢淫佚，載籍所無。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, memorialists argued that Cai You had launched the Yan Mountain campaign, bringing calamity on the realm, and was arrogant, extravagant, and debauched beyond anything recorded in history.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month critics charged that Cai You had launched the Yan Mountain campaign, bringing disaster on the empire, and had indulged in arrogance and debauchery unmatched in the historical record.

sentences.zh: 詔誅攸? 弟翛。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the execution of You? and his younger brother Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the execution of Cai You and his younger brother Cai Xiao.

sentences.zh: 高宗承大亂之後，治王時雍等賣國之罪，洪芻、余大均、陳沖、張卿才、李彝、王及之、周懿文、胡思文並下御史臺獄。

translations.literal: After the great disorder, Gaozong punished Wang Shiyong and others for selling out the state; Hong Chu, Yu Dajun, Chen Chong, Zhang Qingcai, Li Yi, Wang Jizhi, Zhou Yiwen, and Hu Siwen were all sent to the Censorate prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the cataclysm, Gaozong moved against Wang Shiyong and others for betraying the dynasty. Hong Chu, Yu Dajun, Chen Chong, Zhang Qingcai, Li Yi, Wang Jizhi, Zhou Yiwen, and Hu Siwen were all thrown into Censorate custody.

sentences.zh: 獄具，刑寺論芻納景王寵姬，大均納喬貴妃侍兒，及之苦辱寧德皇后女弟，當流；

translations.literal: When the case was complete, the Penal Bureau ruled that Chu had taken a favored concubine of the Prince of Jing, Dajun had taken a maid of Consort Qiao, and Jizhi had cruelly humiliated the younger sister of Empress Ningde—all deserving exile;
translations.idiomatic: When the investigation concluded, the Penal Bureau found that Chu had taken a favored concubine of the Prince of Jing, Dajun a maid of Consort Qiao, and Jizhi had brutally humiliated the Empress of Ningde's younger sister—all warranting exile;

sentences.zh: 沖括金銀自盜，與宮人飲，當絞；

translations.literal: Chong had seized gold and silver for himself and drank with palace women—deserving strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: Chong had plundered gold and silver for himself and caroused with palace women—warranting strangulation;

sentences.zh: 懿文、卿才、彝與宮人飲，卿才、彝當徒，懿文當杖；

translations.literal: Yiwen, Qingcai, and Yi drank with palace women—Qingcai and Yi deserving penal servitude, Yiwen deserving beating;
translations.idiomatic: Yiwen, Qingcai, and Yi had drunk with palace women—Qingcai and Yi were sentenced to penal servitude, Yiwen to beating;

sentences.zh: 思文於推擇張邦昌狀內添諂奉之詞，罰銅十斤：並該赦。

translations.literal: Siwen had added flattering words in the memorial recommending Zhang Bangchang, fined ten catties of copper: all were covered by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Siwen had inserted sycophantic language into the memorial recommending Zhang Bangchang and was fined ten catties of copper—all were eligible for amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上閱狀大怒，李綱等共解之，上亦新政，重於殺士大夫，乃詔芻、大均、沖各特貸命，流沙門島，永不放還；

translations.literal: The Emperor, reading the report, was greatly angered; Li Gang and others jointly interceded; the Emperor was also newly ruling and reluctant to kill scholar-officials, and therefore ordered Chu, Dajun, and Chong each specially spared from death and exiled to Shamen Island, never to be released;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reading the report, flew into a rage. Li Gang and others pleaded on the defendants' behalf. Still establishing his rule and reluctant to execute scholar-officials, he commuted the death sentences of Chu, Dajun, and Chong and exiled them to Shamen Island, never to return;

sentences.zh: 卿才、彝、及之、懿文、思文並以別駕安置邊郡。

translations.literal: Qingcai, Yi, Jizhi, Yiwen, and Siwen were all assigned as vice prefects to border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Qingcai, Yi, Jizhi, Yiwen, and Siwen were all posted as vice prefects to frontier districts.

sentences.zh: 宋齊愈下臺獄，法寺以犯在五月一日赦前，奏裁。

translations.literal: Song Qiyu was sent to the Censorate prison; the Penal Bureau reported that the offense occurred before the amnesty of the first day of the fifth month and submitted for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiyu was thrown into Censorate custody. The Penal Bureau noted that his offense predated the May first amnesty and submitted the case for imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 詔齊愈謀立異姓，以危宗社，非受偽命臣僚之比，特不赦，腰斬都市。

translations.literal: An edict said Qiyu had plotted to establish a person of another surname, endangering the altars of state—not comparable to officials who had accepted false commissions; he was specially excluded from amnesty and cut in two at the waist in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that Qiyu had plotted to install a ruler of another surname, threatening the dynasty itself—not comparable to officials who had merely accepted appointments from a puppet regime. He was expressly denied amnesty and executed by waist-slicing in the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔東京及行在官擅離任者，並就本處根勘之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that officials of the Eastern Capital and the mobile court who had left their posts without authorization were all to be investigated at their locations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a full investigation of every official in the Eastern Capital and the mobile court who had abandoned his post without authorization.

sentences.zh: 淮寧守趙子崧，靖康末，傳檄四方，語頗不遜。

translations.literal: Zhao Zisong, prefect of Huaining, at the end of Jingkang circulated proclamations to the four directions with language rather insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zisong, prefect of Huaining, circulated proclamations across the realm at the end of the Jingkang crisis in language that bordered on insubordination.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔御史置獄京口鞫之。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered the censors to establish a prison at Jingkou and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict ordered the censors to set up a tribunal at Jingkou and investigate him.

sentences.zh: 情得，帝不欲暴其罪，以棄鎮江罪貶南雄州。

translations.literal: The facts were established; the Emperor did not wish to expose his crimes and demoted him to Nanxiong Prefecture on the charge of abandoning Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the facts were established, the emperor declined to publicize his full offenses and demoted him to Nanxiong on the lesser charge of abandoning Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年四月，苗傅等疾閹宦恣橫，及聞王淵為樞密，愈不平，乃與王世脩謀逆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Jianyan, Miao Fu and others resented the eunuchs' unrestrained arrogance; when they heard Wang Yuan had become Military Affairs Commissioner they were still more aggrieved, and together with Wang Shixiu plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Jianyan 3, Miao Fu and his allies, already furious at the eunuchs' unchecked arrogance, grew still more incensed when Wang Yuan was made Military Affairs Commissioner. They joined Wang Shixiu in plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔御史捕世脩鞫之，斬於市。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the censors to arrest Shixiu, interrogate him, and behead him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the censors to arrest Shixiu, try him, and execute him in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 七月，韓世忠執苗傅等，磔之建康。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Han Shizhong seized Miao Fu and the others and dismembered them at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Han Shizhong captured Miao Fu and his co-conspirators and had them dismembered at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 統制王德擅殺軍將陳彥章，臺鞫當死，帝以其有戰功，特貸之。

translations.literal: Wang De, regimental commander, had on his own authority killed army officer Chen Yanzhang; the censors tried him and he deserved death, but the Emperor, because he had battle merit, specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commander Wang De had executed army officer Chen Yanzhang on his own authority. The censors found him deserving of death, but the emperor spared him in recognition of his battlefield service.

sentences.zh: 慶遠軍節度使范瓊領兵入見，面對不遜。

translations.literal: Fan Qiong, Military Commissioner of Qingyuan, led troops to an audience and was insubordinate in his replies.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong, military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army, led his troops to an audience and answered the throne insolently.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院張浚奏瓊大逆不道，付大理寺鞫之，獄具，賜死。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Jun memorialized that Qiong was guilty of great rebellion and iniquity; he was handed to the Court of Judicial Review for interrogation, and when the case was complete he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Jun charged Qiong with treason. Handed over to the Court of Judicial Review, he was sentenced to death by imperial order once the case was complete.

sentences.zh: 越州守郭仲荀，寇至棄城遁，過行在不朝。

translations.literal: Guo Zhongxun, prefect of Yuezhou, when bandits arrived abandoned the city and fled, passing the mobile court without attending audience.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongxun, prefect of Yuezhou, fled when raiders arrived, abandoning his city, and passed the mobile court without presenting himself.

sentences.zh: 付御史臺、大理寺雜治，貶廣州。

translations.literal: He was handed to the Censorate and Court of Judicial Review for joint handling and demoted to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate and Court of Judicial Review jointly tried him, and he was demoted to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 神武軍統制魯珏坐賊殺不辜，掠良家子女，帝以其有戰功，貸之，貶瑞州。

translations.literal: Lu Jue, regimental commander of the Divine Martial Army, was guilty of bandits killing the innocent and seizing good families' sons and daughters; the Emperor, because he had battle merit, pardoned him and demoted him to Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jue, a regimental commander of the Divine Martial Army, was convicted of letting his troops murder innocents and seize civilians' children. The emperor spared his life in view of his military service and demoted him to Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，監察御史婁寅亮陳宗社大計，奏檜惡之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, Supervising Censor Lou Yinliang set forth the great plan for altars of state; Qin Hui hated his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1, Supervising Censor Lou Yinliang memorialized on the survival of the dynasty—a memorial Qin Hui detested.

sentences.zh: 十一月，使言者論其父死匿不舉哀，下大理寺劾治，迄無所得，詔免所居官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he had memorialists argue that when his father died he concealed it and did not observe mourning; he was sent to the Court of Judicial Review for impeachment and investigation, but nothing was found; an edict removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Qin Hui had critics charge that Lou had concealed his father's death and failed to observe mourning. The case went to the Court of Judicial Review but turned up nothing; an edict stripped Lou of his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，樞密使張俊使人誣張憲，謂收岳飛文字謀為變。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun had men falsely accuse Zhang Xian, saying he had received Yue Fei's writings plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Military Affairs Commissioner Zhang Jun had agents frame Zhang Xian, claiming he had received correspondence from Yue Fei plotting a mutiny.

sentences.zh: 秦檜欲乘此誅飛，命万俟 鍛鍊成之。

translations.literal: Qin Hui wished to seize on this to execute Fei and ordered Wan Qi to forge the case to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui meant to use the case to destroy Yue Fei and ordered Wan Qixie to fabricate the charges until the conviction held.

sentences.zh: 飛賜死，誅其子雲及憲于市。

translations.literal: Fei was granted death; his son Yun and Xian were executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei was executed by imperial order; his son Yun and Zhang Xian were put to death in public.

sentences.zh: 汾州進士智浹上書訟飛 ，決杖編管袁州。

translations.literal: Zhi Xia, a presented scholar of Fenzhou, submitted a memorial pleading Fei's case; he was sentenced to beating with the rod and registered supervision at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Xia, a presented scholar from Fenzhou, memorialized in Yue Fei's defense. He was beaten with the rod and exiled under registered supervision to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣西帥胡舜陟與轉運使呂源有隙，源奏舜陟贓污僭擬，又以書抵檜，言舜陟訕笑朝政。

translations.literal: Hu Shunzhi, commander of Guangxi, had a rift with Transport Commissioner Lü Yuan; Yuan memorialized that Shunzhi was corrupt and presumptuous in imitating imperial style, and also wrote to Hui saying Shunzhi mocked and laughed at court policy.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shunzhi, military commander of Guangxi, feuded with transport commissioner Lü Yuan. Yuan accused Shunzhi of corruption and arrogating imperial prerogatives, and wrote separately to Qin Hui claiming Shunzhi ridiculed court policy.

sentences.zh: 檜素惡舜陟，遣大理官往治之。

translations.literal: Hui had long hated Shunzhi and dispatched Court of Judicial Review officials to handle the case.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had long despised Shunzhi and sent officials from the Court of Judicial Review to prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，舜陟不服，死於獄。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year, Shunzhi did not confess and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year Shunzhi refused to confess and died in custody.

sentences.zh: 飛與舜陟死，檜權愈熾，屢興大獄以中異己者，名曰詔獄，實非詔旨也。

translations.literal: After the deaths of Fei and Shunzhi, Hui's power grew ever fiercer; he repeatedly raised great cases to strike down those who differed from him, calling them imperial prisons by edict though in fact there was no edict.
translations.idiomatic: After the deaths of Yue Fei and Hu Shunzhi, Qin Hui's power grew unchecked. He repeatedly opened major prosecutions to destroy opponents, calling them "imperial prisons by edict" though no such edicts existed.

sentences.zh: 其後所謂詔獄，紛紛類此，故不備錄云。

translations.literal: The so-called imperial prisons by edict that followed were numerous and of this kind; therefore they are not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The pseudo-imperial prisons that followed were too numerous and too much alike to record in full.
